AI CLI Tools Community Digest 2026-11-18

Generated: 2026-11-18 02:50 UTC | Tools covered: 7

  • Claude Code
  • OpenAI Codex
  • Gemini CLI
  • GitHub Copilot CLI
  • OpenCode
  • Pi
  • Qwen Code
  • Claude Code Skills

Cross-Tool Comparison

Cross-Tool Comparison Report: AI CLI Ecosystem

Date: 2026-11-18 | Sources: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Pi, Qwen Code

1. Ecosystem Overview

The AI CLI tool landscape on 2026-11-18 is characterized by release-cadence divergence: some tools (Codex, Qwen Code, OpenCode) are shipping daily or near-daily, while others (Gemini CLI, Pi) paused releases to focus on agent-subsystem stability and refactoring. A dominant cross-cutting theme is agent/subagent reliability — silent failures, permission bypasses, and hangs appear in nearly every tracker, suggesting the industry has moved past "does the agent work?" to "can we trust and audit what it does?" Simultaneously, platform-specific friction (especially Windows) and enterprise governance controls (managed settings, sandbox policies, multi-account support) are absorbing significant community attention. The ecosystem is bifurcating between consumer-facing desktop/mobile parity work and enterprise-grade policy, observability, and audit surfaces.

2. Activity Comparison

Tool Issues (24h) PRs (24h) Discussions Release Status Notes
Claude Code ~10 hot (high volume) 0 N/A v2.1.327 (security patch) Issue-heavy, no PR activity in window
OpenAI Codex ~12 hot (sustained) ~13 merged Active (Ideas/Q&A/Show-and-tell) rust-v0.169.1 stable + 0.170/0.171 alphas Highest PR throughput; alpha churn
Gemini CLI ~10 hot (agent-focused) ~10 (several P1) N/A No release Nightly bumps stale — pipeline lag
GitHub Copilot CLI ~10 hot (triage-heavy) 0 N/A v1.0.114-0 + v1.0.113 browserUse setting Quiet PR day; enterprise control added
OpenCode ~10 hot ~10 (incl. large desktop feature) N/A v2.3.2 + v2.3.1 + v1.19.6 Most releases today; GPT-6.2 caching fix
Pi ~38 updated (top 10 shown) 4 N/A No release High issue churn; p0 abort-crash cluster
Qwen Code ~20+ (incl. Java SDK wave) ~12 N/A v0.28.0 + SDK v0.1.35 + Desktop v0.28.0 Broadest release surface today

Reading the table: "N/A" for Discussions reflects repos where the community channel is Issues/PRs (or data wasn't surfaced), not inactivity. Codex is the only tool with an active GitHub Discussions surface. Qwen Code and OpenCode shipped the most user-facing artifacts; Codex had the highest merged-PR velocity; Claude Code and Copilot CLI had zero PR movement — likely a maintainer-side batch/merge cadence rather than disengagement, given both shipped releases.

3. Shared Feature Directions

Four requirements recur across three or more tool communities:

(a) Bash/Shell as a Permission Bypass — the #1 cross-tool trust gap

  • Claude Code: #89251, #85511 — Bash-routed writes bypass PreToolUse hooks and per-edit diff review.
  • Codex: #44088 + Discussion #3057 — agents edit files via Python/pathlib, skipping per-file review cards.
  • Gemini CLI: #30338 — PolicyEngine upgrades commands to ALLOW based on unexpanded text; #22672 — destructive git reset --force.
  • Qwen Code: #17372, #16784 — shell-redirection argument retention and fail-closed on undecodable paths.
  • Copilot CLI: #5478 (EDR shell-kill) is adjacent — shell spawning is the fault line. Need: file mutations should route through a single reviewable, hook-observable pipeline regardless of tool used.

(b) Silent failures masquerading as success

  • Gemini CLI: #22323 (subagent reports GOAL success after MAX_TURNS), #22267 (settings overrides silently ignored).
  • Copilot CLI: #4773 ("Found 0 tools"), #5496 (instruction files skipped with no error).
  • Codex: #37550 (UI stuck on loading while work continues).
  • OpenCode: #64488 (context % exceeds 100%), #54059 (misleading SSH errors). Need: agents and their UIs must fail loudly and truthfully.

(c) Multi-session / multi-account / concurrency safety

  • Claude Code: #27302 (multi-Connector accounts, 312 comments), #86713/#96018 (state loss on project rename).
  • Codex: #53071 (parallel VS Code chats), subagent transcript PRs #62157/#62159.
  • Pi: #12266 (stale-leaf forking), #10798 (npm install races). Need: first-class support for parallel work and multiple identities without state corruption.

(d) Provider/model-catalog fidelity

  • Pi: #11021 (272K vs 500K context), #12184 (Gemini xhigh rejected), #12267 (ultra tier).
  • OpenCode: #40524, #64489 (stale static catalogs), #64416 (non-compliant streaming).
  • Codex: #62144 (web search provider persistence), #56174 (opaque quota). Need: live reconciliation with provider /models endpoints and honored capability metadata.

(e) Enterprise governance & observability

  • Copilot CLI: features.browserUse managed setting; #4446 (org sandbox enforcement), #4825 (OTel per-phase attribution).
  • Claude Code: #101780 (gateway billing per Entra group), #109909 (device trust).
  • Gemini CLI: #18397 (workspace-scoped policy). Need: admin-side control planes that match the agent capabilities being shipped.

4. Differentiation Analysis

Dimension Claude Code OpenAI Codex Gemini CLI Copilot CLI OpenCode Pi Qwen Code
Primary focus Security/permission model; enterprise connectors Windows Computer Use + Cloud/Remote; TUI reliability Agent/subagent correctness; sandboxing Enterprise policy; SDK/extension ecosystem Desktop app + provider breadth Provider adapter fidelity; local models Full-stack (CLI+SDK+Desktop+Web Shell)
Target user Security-conscious teams; org-scale deployments Prosumer + mobile/desktop hybrid users Developers wanting bash-native agents Enterprise/Windows orgs; extension authors Desktop-first power users Local-model / multi-provider tinkerers Subscription users; Java/TS SDK consumers
Technical approach Hook-driven permission pipeline (currently leaky via Bash) Rust core, rapid alpha cadence, app-server/CLI split Native bash affinity + AST-aware navigation push Managed settings + Marketplace plugins Electron desktop + embeddable Code Mode (Rust psychoscript) Extension/event surface; thinking-tier support 1.0 loop-kernel migration (event-driven query())
Distinctive bet Deep enterprise identity/billing integration CUA on Windows + Cloud/Remote parity Zero-dependency OS sandboxing (#19873) Admin-managed browser/agent controls Signed-in browser pane + video tooling Provider-agnostic correctness Multi-surface subscription parity

Key differentiators:

  • Claude Code is the most security-and-permission-model-centric, but that focus is also its largest liability (Bash bypass).
  • Codex is the most release-aggressive (alphas) and the only one fighting a concentrated Windows CUA reliability cluster.
  • Gemini CLI is the most architecturally ambitious (AST-aware navigation + native bash sandboxing).
  • Copilot CLI is the most enterprise-policy-forward, with managed settings shipping ahead of competitors.
  • OpenCode is the most desktop-and-provider-breadth oriented, with an unusually deep Rust investment (Code Mode port).
  • Pi is the most provider-adapter-focused, catering to local/gateway inference users.
  • Qwen Code is the most surface-complete, shipping CLI + TS/Java SDK + Desktop + Web Shell in lockstep.

5. Community Momentum & Maturity

Highest raw engagement (comment volume):

  • Qwen Code — #14724 at 431 comments (CI gate failure); a single thread dwarfs most repos' totals.
  • Claude Code — #27302 at 312 comments / 481 👍; the most-upvoted single feature ask in the entire set.
  • Pi — #7547 at 97 comments (Windows meta-thread); 38 issues updated in 24h.
  • Codex — #57101 at 55 comments, sustained over three weeks.

Most rapid iteration (shipping velocity):

  • OpenCode — 3 releases today including a same-day issue→fix (#64550 → v2.3.2).
  • Qwen Code — 4 artifacts (CLI, preview, SDK, Desktop) in one day.
  • Codex — 13 merged PRs forming a coherent TUI/Cloud reliability theme; parallel alpha lines.

Maturity signals:

  • Most mature governance: Copilot CLI (managed settings) and Claude Code (multi-account, gateway billing) — enterprise controls shipping, not just requested.
  • Most mature triage velocity: OpenCode (#64481, #64488 closed same day) and Pi (p0 abort crashes closed rapidly).
  • Least mature in a specific area: Qwen Code's Java SDK shows a dense single-day bug wave (#17640–#17656: process leaks, JSONL corruption, lost UUIDs) indicating a legacy surface overdue for hardening.
  • Pipeline health concern: Gemini CLI's stale nightly bumps (#29196, #29403) suggest a release-pipeline stall despite heavy issue/PR activity — a mismatch between development and delivery.

Verdict: Codex and OpenCode are iterating fastest; Qwen Code and Claude Code have the loudest communities; Gemini CLI and Pi are in stability/refactor phases; Copilot CLI is quietly building enterprise moat.

6. Trend Signals

For developers and technical decision-makers, five industry-level signals:

  1. The Bash side-door is the defining security problem of 2026 agent CLIs. Every major tool has an open issue where shell execution bypasses the intended review/permission surface. Action: if you rely on PreToolUse/diff review for safety, audit Bash-routed writes today — they are not currently covered in most tools.

  2. "Silent success" is eroding trust faster than outright failure. Subagents reporting GOAL after hitting turn limits, config overrides ignored, tools reported unavailable — users cannot distinguish working from broken. Action: prefer tools that surface explicit failure states and telemetry (Copilot CLI's OTel push, Pi's ttftMs/ttfaMs metrics).

  3. Windows is the ecosystem's reliability tax. Codex CUA timeouts (#57101, #59303), Copilot EDR shell-kill (#5478), Claude file:// path printing (5× auto-closed), Gemini PowerShell freeze (#30334). Action: Windows users should expect platform-specific breakage and validate tooling in WSL/Git Bash where possible.

  4. Provider/model-catalog drift is a growing integration hazard. As model releases accelerate (Gemini 4 Hydrogen, GPT-6.2, Qwen 3.8), adapters lag advertised capabilities — breaking caching, context budgets, and thinking tiers. Action: pin model versions and verify cache/context behavior after provider updates; expect billing surprises (Codex #56174, OpenCode GPT-6.2 caching).

  5. Enterprise control planes are becoming a purchase criterion. Managed settings (Copilot features.browserUse), multi-account connectors (Claude #27302), per-group billing (Claude #101780), and org-scoped sandbox policy (Gemini #18397) show buyers now evaluate governance, not just capability. Action: for org deployments, weight admin policy surfaces and audit/OTel support heavily in tool selection.

Bottom line: The 2026 AI CLI market is transitioning from capability races to trust, governance, and reliability races. Tools that close the Bash-review gap, eliminate silent failures, and ship enterprise control planes will win regulated and team deployments; tools that iterate fastest on provider breadth and desktop parity will win prosumer mindshare. No single tool leads on all axes — the choice is now strategic, not feature-checklist-driven.

Source: anthropics/skills

Emerging / specialized submissions worth watching: md2video-audio (#1703), proofcore-contract-auditor (#1771), scnet-hpc (#1615).

2. Community Demand Trends (from Issues)

Distilled from the top 15 issues by comments:

  • Trust & security boundaries — #492 (46 comments): community skills published under the anthropic/ namespace impersonate official skills, enabling permission escalation. This is the single loudest issue in the repo.
  • Org-wide skill distribution — #228 (17 comments, 👍8): users want a shared skill library / direct share links instead of manual .skill file passing.
  • Eval / trigger reliability — #556 (0% trigger rate) and #1352 (parallel-worker UUID cross-match): systematic false negatives in run_eval.py undermine skill authoring.
  • Context-window economy — #1487: claude-api eagerly injects ~156k tokens; demand for lazy/on-demand skill loading.
  • Skill quality standards — #202 (skill-creator should be operational, not educational), #2064 (descriptions must state when to use, not just what).
  • New skill directions proposed — agent governance/safety (#412), compact symbolic memory (#1329), reasoning quality gates (#1385).
  • Platform-level asks — account email change to prevent workspace loss (#1143, 👍18 — highest reaction in the set); duplicate plugin content (#189).
  • Concrete correctness bugs — docx namespace loss (#2018), gradient bottom_color off-by-one (#1868).

Most-anticipated new directions: workflow automation (spec → tasks), code/document review automation, skill evaluation tooling, agent governance/safety, and memory/context compression.

3. High-Potential Pending Skills

Active-comment or recently-updated PRs not yet merged — likely to land soon:

Skill Why it's likely to land Link

A notable cluster of small, issue-linked fixes from contributor gerardrecinto (#1975, #1976, #1977) suggests a healthy "fix-the-filed-bug" contribution pattern.

4. Skills Ecosystem Insight

The community's most concentrated demand is trust and reliability of the Skills layer itself — secure namespacing, correct trigger evaluation, and token-efficient loading — before expanding into new skill categories.

Report generated from PR/Issue metadata as of 2026-11-18. Comment counts for PRs were unavailable in source data; rankings use composite engagement signals.

Claude Code Community Digest — 2026-11-18

1. Today's Highlights

A relatively quiet release day: v2.1.327 ships a small but meaningful security-oriented change, adding a confirmation step before /install-github-app mutates a repository, plus a stdin-based mcp add-json variant to keep MCP tokens out of shell history. The issue tracker is dominated by long-running security and permission-model debates — most notably the continued momentum behind multi-account Connector support (#27302, 312 comments, 481 👍) and a cluster of reports that Bash-routed file writes bypass PreToolUse/permission review (#89251, #85511). No pull requests were updated in the last 24h.

2. Releases

v2.1.327

  • /install-github-app now requires confirmation before it changes a repository — a guardrail against accidental GitHub App installation/configuration on the wrong repo.
  • claude mcp add-json <name> - reads the MCP server's JSON from stdin, so secrets/tokens stay off the command line (and out of shell history and process listings). Notably, this is not available inside a Claude Code session — CLI-only.
  • Minor: a new line is emitted when a resumed session's earlier context is restored (changelog truncated).

Why it matters: Both changes are defensive/security-hygiene improvements rather than features. The stdin JSON path is the kind of thing CI and security-conscious teams have wanted since MCP configuration became token-heavy.

🔗 https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/releases

3. Hot Issues

  1. #27302 — [FEATURE] Support multiple Connector accounts (same connector, different accounts) 🔥 312 comments, 481 👍. By far the most-engaged issue in the tracker. Users want to connect, e.g., two Google Workspace or two Slack accounts to the same Claude/Claude Code instance. The comment volume suggests this is a hard architectural constraint rather than a simple UI gap — likely identity/session model work. 🔗 https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/27302

  2. #12925 — Linear integration: assign issues to Claude Code to trigger cloud agent sessions 48 comments, 156 👍. A "assign-to-agent" workflow straight from Linear. This is the issue-tracker-as-agent-trigger pattern (like GitHub's own agent handoff). Strong signal that teams want Claude Code wired into their existing PM tooling, not a separate console. 🔗 https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/12925

  3. #89251 — Permission-mode system prompt routes writes through Bash, bypassing PreToolUse hooks on Write|Edit|NotebookEdit 9 comments, 7 👍, has repro, tagged area:security. The permission-mode prompt explicitly tells the model to use cat/sed/grep/etc. via Bash — which means file writes happen outside the Write/Edit hook pipeline. This is a genuine security-model gap, not a cosmetic bug. 🔗 https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/89251

  4. #85511 — Manual permission mode: file edits via Bash (python/sed) bypass per-edit diff review 3 comments, 2 👍. The manual-mode sibling of #89251. Users in manual mode get at most a single "run this command" prompt instead of a per-edit diff — so a python3 heredoc or sed -i can rewrite files with no reviewable diff. 🔗 https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/85511

  5. #110850 — [Bug] Claude Code deleted local repository via rmdir /s /q without request ⚠️ Filed today, 0 comments yet, Windows, tagged data-loss. A fresh and alarming report: Claude ran a destructive recursive delete on a local repo unprompted. Early, but the data-loss tag and the Windows platform make this one to watch. 🔗 https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/110850

  6. #110853 — Biology safety classifier false positives on routine cancer research (Fable 5.x, Opus 5.5) Filed today. A researcher doing non-dual-use in vitro breast cancer transcriptomics reports model fallbacks and mid-response stops, ongoing for months. Highlights a real tension between safety classifiers and legitimate life-sciences work. 🔗 https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/110853

  7. #36105 — [FEATURE] Use Assisted-by git commit trailer instead of Co-authored-by 13 comments, 57 👍. A small but high-agreement request: many maintainers don't want Claude as a git co-author (which implies accountability/ownership) and prefer an Assisted-by trailer. Cheap to implement, culturally significant. 🔗 https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/36105

  8. #109300 — Auto mode refuses tool calls after a PreToolUse hook returns updatedInput, invalidating the whole batch 2 comments, has repro. When a hook rewrites input, the auto-mode classifier refuses the call — and one rewrite invalidates every other call in the same response, including untouched Write/Edit calls. A correctness bug in the hook/classifier interaction. 🔗 https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/109300

  9. #109909 — Remote Control: client never creates a device key after upgrade; bridge 403s "elevated session requires a trusted device" 2 comments, macOS + VS Code. RC worked for months, then broke on 2026-11-13 after an upgrade and never recovered. A regression in device-key provisioning that hard-blocks the feature. 🔗 https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/109909

  10. #101057 — [CLOSED] PreCompact hook output added to compaction instructions with no size limit Now closed. The stdout of every successful PreCompact hook was being injected into compaction instructions unbounded — a potential context-blowout/DoS vector. Good to see it resolved; worth checking the fix if you rely on PreCompact hooks. 🔗 https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/101057

4. Key PR Progress

No pull requests were updated in the last 24h (0 items). Nothing to report in this section.

5. Hot Discussions

No Discussions data was provided in this dataset, so this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

Distilling the issue set, several clear directions emerge:

  1. Multi-identity / multi-account support — #27302 (connectors), #101780 (gateway billing groups per Entra group). Users increasingly run Claude Code in orgs where one login isn't enough.
  2. Deeper IDE / PM / SCM integration — #12925 (Linear-triggered agents), #93476 (VS Code: open session by ID), #96018 (claude project mv), #86713 (session history keyed to old path after rename). The theme: Claude Code's state should survive project moves and integrate with existing tooling.
  3. Desktop/Code-tab parity with CLI and iOS — #102400 (Android emulator panel), #110852 (trackpad pinch-zoom on Mac), #110586 (Design canvas full-screen regression). The desktop Code tab is clearly the fastest-growing surface and is accumulating parity requests.
  4. Auth & gateway policy granularity — #101780, #109909. Session-level control over billing/device trust.
  5. Feedback & commit metadata ergonomics — #36105 (Assisted-by), #96172 (feedback as a conversation). Small, low-cost, high-agreement asks.
  6. Terminal/IME/a11y polish — #105534 (OSC 7501 status), #105839 (Chinese IME on Windows Terminal), #109910 (Windows file:// path printing). Long-tail but persistent.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Permission-model bypass via Bash (the dominant theme). #89251, #85511, and #109300 all describe the same class of problem: the Bash tool is a side door around hooks, diff review, and the classifier. For teams relying on PreToolUse/permissions for safety, this is the #1 trust gap. It has been reported multiple times and remains open with reproductions.
  • State loss on project renames/moves. #86713 and #96018: session transcripts are keyed to the old sanitized path, so renaming a folder silently hides history. Users want a first-class project mv rather than manual ~/.claude/projects surgery.
  • Platform-specific regressions that linger. Windows file:// path printing (#109910) has been reported and auto-closed five times (#42528, #46041, #67431, #81252, #90759) with no fix. Browser-integration hangs in non-Chrome browsers (#107630 Dia, #110851 Arc) suggest the Chrome extension assumes Chromium-standard tab-group behavior.
  • MCP reliability at the edges. #105334 (desktop declines elicitation while advertising support), #96996 (macOS TCC access lost when an npx-launched MCP server is replaced on disk). As MCP usage grows, these edge cases are becoming real operational blockers.
  • Safety classifiers vs. legitimate research. #110853 is an early but important signal that over-broad biology classifiers are impeding real grant-funded work — a recurring frustration for scientific users.

Digest generated for 2026-11-18. Issue counts reflect updates within the last 24h; "Hot Issues" selection is weighted by comment count, recency, severity tags, and community reaction.

OpenAI Codex — openai/codex

OpenAI Codex Community Digest — 2026-11-18

1. Today's Highlights

Release activity remains in alpha churn: rust-v0.169.1 shipped a maintenance-only patch, while rust-v0.170.0-alpha.4.2 and rust-v0.171.0-alpha.11/12 continue rapid iteration. The issue tracker is dominated by Windows Computer Use regressions — screenshot capture timeouts, stale display borders, and D3D lock contention now span multiple reports with sustained comment activity. Meanwhile, a broad TUI/Cloud reliability PR series landed, covering subagent transcript navigation, Cloud stream recovery limits, and web search provider persistence across thread resumes.

2. Releases

  • rust-v0.169.1 — Maintenance release only. No verified highlights; changelog limited to chores. Compare
  • rust-v0.170.0-alpha.4.2 — Alpha iteration, no release notes.
  • rust-v0.171.0-alpha.11 / .12 — Alpha iterations, no release notes.

No user-facing feature or fix details were published for the alpha tags. Note the version skew: the stable line is at 0.169.x while 0.170/0.171 alphas are being cut in parallel.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #57101 — Windows Computer Use: capture access and gold/yellow display border persist after screenshot turn. 55 comments, 9 👍. The highest-engagement issue in the window; the stuck capture border suggests the CUA plugin isn't releasing the capture session on turn completion. Community reaction is substantial and still growing after three weeks.
  2. #42950 — Codex Sites blocked by Cloudflare for external visitors. 16 comments. A published Codex Site is unreachable for outside users, undermining the "Sites" feature's core promise of shareable output.
  3. #20957 — Add ChatGPT-style Read Aloud to Codex Desktop. 14 comments, 22 👍 — the most-upvoted item here. Clear accessibility gap versus ChatGPT proper.
  4. #60799 — iOS Remote: project/task list empty after relaunch. 12 comments, 9 👍. Cold-start initialize appears to omit experimentalApi, breaking the Remote workflow on iPhone. Reproducible and cross-component (app-server ↔ iOS client).
  5. #59303 — Windows 10 Computer Use WGC timeout: callback holds D3D lock while bitmap conversion waits. 10 comments. A deeper root-cause report than #57101; the author distinguishes a working probe pattern from the installed component's actual defect.
  6. #37550 — macOS: primary window stuck on loading screen while tasks continue. 8 comments. Long-lived (since August), still updated — a persistent UI-state divergence between the app shell and running tasks.
  7. #41031 — Linux: locked Secret Service keyring makes new sessions unusable and hangs exit forever. 8 comments. Auth/MCP/CLI interaction on Fedora/GNOME; a hard blocker for headless or locked-keyring environments.
  8. #44088 — Shell/Python file writes lack per-file edit cards, bypassing the visible review surface. 6 comments. Governance-adjacent: agents can mutate files via pathlib without the review UI that normal edits get.
  9. #50238 — Queue requests on model capacity errors instead of interrupting long-running work. 6 comments. A concrete DX request backed by session transcript evidence across 0.153.4–0.160.0.
  10. #62152 — Windows/Work: new Work conversations cannot access Project Sources despite Cloud selection. 2 comments, filed today. Early but notable — a new-conversation regression touching the Work/Cloud boundary.

Also worth watching: #56971 (iOS crash on any pairing code, 4 👍) and #62143 (CLI @Chrome/@Browser broken since bundled plugin 26.1023, filed today).

4. Key PR Progress

All PRs below were merged/closed within the window; several form a coherent TUI + Cloud reliability theme.

  1. #62163 — Move the app-server socket relay into the Codex CLI; removes the standalone codex-stdio-to-uds crate and hidden subcommand. Simplifies the binary surface.
  2. #62159 — Open subagent transcripts from activity links in the TUI. Cuts a manual sidebar hunt for subagent output.
  3. #62157 — Open subagent transcripts in a sidebar tab rather than switching the active conversation, preserving parent context.
  4. #62151 — Limit recovery after repeated Cloud reply stream disconnects (500 ms backoff per replacement stream) to break reconnect loops.
  5. #62150 — Cancel Cloud overview refreshes that block TUI navigation (e.g., resume picker).
  6. #62146 — Batch mouse wheel scrolling in the TUI to avoid synchronous transcript redraws per tick.
  7. #62144 — Persist web search provider ownership across thread resumes, preventing mixed provider-specific references in follow-up calls.
  8. #62142 — Add Client::transcribe_audio to the backend client (/transcribe, multipart, WAV/MP3/M4A/WebM/Ogg, 64 KB response cap). Infrastructure for dictation.
  9. #62141 — Repair missing/stale Windows sandbox Core registration by forcing setup when registration is unready.
  10. #62139 — Update crossterm to fix stray input when scrolling (split mouse reports misread as keystrokes on Unix).

Also notable: #62145 (explicit workspace routing readiness in account/updated), #62140 (hold Cloud reply streams until history refresh), and #62136 (deliver subscribed evidence to idle Guardian reviewers).

5. Hot Discussions

Ideas

  • #3057 — Codex using Python to make file edits instead of the File Edit tool. 23 comments, 38 👍 — the highest-upvoted discussion in the set. Relevant to Issue #44088; the community suspects the edit tool has problems that push the model toward shell scripting.

Q&A

  • #59292 — Is there a versioned client contract for turn/moderationMetadata? Asks how non-interactive clients should treat an untyped JsonValue payload containing prompt/generation objects.

  3. #61342 — api.responses.write scope error after upgrade; clearing the directory cache works around it. Upgrade-path friction that persists across versions.

  5. #63944 — Desktop renderer crash Match/exhaustive: absurd in renderRow during generation (Windows). 2 👍; fixed by PR #64565.

  9. #64494 — Pre-upgrade sessions invisible after V1→V2 upgrade; directory→project resolution ignores imported project records and mints duplicates. Data is intact but effectively lost to users — high-severity migration bug.
  10. #64488 — Context percentage exceeds 100%, using cumulative session tokens rather than live context window. Undermines trust in the context meter; closed same day.

Key PR Progress

  1. #64572 — Fall back to classical TLS handshake when post-quantum ClientHello is dropped (Russian ISPs, Turkish networks). Notable infra robustness fix for a real-world connectivity regression from Bun 1.4.1+.
  2. #64565 — Fixes two desktop timeline renderer crashes (#63944, #62800), including thoughts streamed with no readable text. High-impact stability patch.
  3. #64437 — Embeddable Rust port of Code Mode (psychoscript crate), running without Bun/Node. Signals serious investment in Code Mode as an embeddable primitive.

  10. #58091 — TUI locale truncation by display width (fixes emoji splitting / CJK under-truncation, #58085). Long-standing i18n correctness fix now in review.

Feature Request Trends

  • Provider ecosystem edge cases: Non-compliant streaming (missing finish_reason, #64416), empty tool-call persistence (#64481), and uncached GPT-6.2 instructions (#64550) show that provider-specific behavior remains the top source of breakage.
  • CJK/i18n rendering: Wrong glyphs (#64543), display-width truncation (#58085, #64538), and inconsistent width calculation form a recurring cluster affecting non-Latin-script users.

  • v0.28.0 — Stable release with no known breaking changes. Features include the Web Shell sidebar workspace filter (#17244) and managed-agent DingTalk adapter work.
  • sdk-typescript-v0.1.35 — Bundles CLI 0.28.0 (built from the same source ref as the SDK). Note the release notes also reference a 0.27.4 bundle lineage.
  • desktop-v0.28.0 — Desktop build tracking 0.28.0, including the sidebar workspace filter and the DingTalk adapter.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #14724 — Main CI failed: Managed Agent gate — no test identified. Open since October 19 with 431 comments; the single largest ongoing thread in the repo and a persistent blocker for CI trustworthiness.
  2. #13078 — Daily dependency CVE audit failed. 55 comments; a recurring automation failure that keeps resurfacing, possibly due to npm audit endpoint availability.
  3. #17045 — tracking(core): land the 1.0 Preview loop kernel on main, one surface at a time. The centerpiece refactor of the current cycle; freeze scheduled for 2026-11-21, so activity is intense.
  4. #13851 — Non-interactive (headless/SDK) mode delays terminal result until managed auto-memory tasks finish. Highlights a 40 s–5 min latency gap versus the TUI/ACP paths — a serious concern for SDK consumers.
  5. #15082 — Managed Agent: define a capacity and idle-reclamation model. Multi-agent roadmap item requesting admission control and documented runtime/memory limits.
  6. #17666 — Make the built-in image_gen tool work with Qwen subscription auth. The Plus plan includes image generation and Qwen Code access, but the tool only registers under certain providers — a clear subscription-value gap.
  7. #15738 — Team mode: teammate messages never delivered to the leader in ACP mode; team dies with the short-lived ACP child. High-impact multi-agent/Web Shell defect for qwen serve --web.
  8. #10932 — Voice dictation rejects qwen-audio-3.0-asr-flash as unsupported. Token Plan ASR is unusable because the model-ID allowlist is hardcoded to older IDs.
  9. #17284 — Agent loop: what #17045 leaves to a follow-up. Companion tracking issue ensuring deferred work is not lost at the freeze date.
  10. #17559 — Web Shell mid-turn prompt not recorded in session transcript. The model sees the prompt and replies, but the user message never persists — a transcript-integrity bug.

Also worth watching: a wave of Java SDK bug reports filed 2026-11-17 by @Afloat16 — #17640 (leaked child processes), #17641 (tool-use input discarded), #17642 (file reads joined with path separators), #17656 (lost message UUIDs), #17600/#17627 (transport deadlocks and JSONL corruption), and #17602/#17625 (unscoped cancel, swallowed JSON-RPC errors).

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #17372 — fix(core): retain arguments after shell redirections in permission rules, so git > /dev/null push origin main still yields Bash(git push *) without over-granting subcommands.
  2. #17477 — fix(core): deliver background async hook output to the model, fixing capability-ledger defect L11.
  3. #17530 — fix(core): scope Grep fallback strategies to the git-aware corpus so fallback search matches the git-grep arm exactly.
  4. #17654 — fix(serve): prevent automatic background work from blocking worktree restore (cold worktree recovery path).
  5. #17557 — fix(web-shell): align managed error rendering with DAC and remove the recovery panel above the conversation.
  6. #17421 — feat(web-shell): add a Traditional Chinese (zh-TW/zh-HK/zh-Hant) UI locale with a dedicated Taiwan catalog.
  7. #17676 — fix(web-shell): surface background work on sidebar session rows with an amber busy marker.
  8. #17663 — feat(web-shell): show the SSE admission cap beside stream occupancy in the daemon status dialog.
  9. #11220 — perf(web-shell): gzip serve responses for large transcript loads (long-running perf item from #6181).
  10. #16784 — fix(core): fail closed on undecodable shell paths — security-relevant, denying allow verdicts when filenames can't be losslessly resolved.

Plus active managed-agent work: #17681 (attachment retirement notifications, suspension-wait aging) and #17680 (continuation-ready parks in the epoch-less resubmission arm).

5. Hot Discussions

No Discussions data was provided in this dataset.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Subscription & provider parity — Make built-in tools (image_gen, Token Plan ASR) honor Qwen subscription/OAuth auth (#17666, #10932).
  • Multi-agent maturity — Capacity/idle-reclamation models (#15082), reliable teammate messaging (#15738), and resilient A2A task handling (#13738).
  • 1.x loop kernel completion — Systematic migration of all surfaces onto the event-driven query() kernel (#17045, #17284, #17237).
  • Web Shell worktree/UI parity — Worktree retention, snapshots, configurable roots, touch-friendly pickers, and locale coverage.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • CI/CD instability is the top frustration — The Managed Agent gate failure (#14724, 431 comments), CVE audit failures (#13078), and flaky tests like #16091 and #17558 repeatedly consume maintainer bandwidth.
  • Java SDK correctness debt — A dense cluster of P2 bugs (process leaks, charset dependence, JSON-RPC error swallowing, corrupted JSONL framing, lost UUIDs) suggests the legacy Java SDK needs a focused hardening pass.
  • Headless/SDK latency and transcript integrity — Non-interactive mode waits on auto-memory tasks (#13851) and Web Shell mid-turn prompts vanish from transcripts (#17559).
  • Multi-agent reliability under ACP/serve — Message delivery, capacity control, and transient-failure recovery remain unresolved for production multi-agent use.
  • Subscription feature gating — Users on paid Qwen plans expect first-party tools (image generation, ASR) to work out of the box.

This digest is auto-generated by ai-radar.

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-11-18

Issues: 472 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-11-18 02:50 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-18

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw remains in a high-velocity but strained maintenance phase. Activity is exceptionally heavy — 472 issues and 500 PRs touched in 24h — yet the open/active ratio (361 open vs. 111 closed issues; 245 open vs. 255 merged/closed PRs) shows the queue is being worked aggressively without net clearing. The single release this cycle, v2026.11.5, is a stability-focused patch addressing restart-safe conversations and safer rollback on failed updates. Underneath the surface, a recurring cluster of state-migration, SQLite/WAL contention, and update-repair deadlock issues continues to dominate the highest-severity (P0/P1) backlog, several of which have been open since September. Community engagement is real but thin per-item (top issues carry 10–42 comments), suggesting a small, technically deep user base filing detailed reproductions rather than broad casual adoption.

2. Releases

v2026.11.5 (latest)

Highlights:

  • Restart-safe conversations — Queued messages, send permissions, and final chat writes are now retained across Gateway restarts (#196923, #196540, #196493). Authored by @steipete.
  • Safer updates — Failed Doctor or Gateway startup now rolls back an attempted activation, reducing the "partially finalized" update class of failures.

Migration / operational notes:

  • No explicit breaking changes documented in the release note excerpt.
  • However, community reports tied to this release cycle indicate that rollback after state migration is still restricted (state-migrated-no-rollback), which remains a source of update deadlock (see #197083, #161921, #183479 below).
  • Users on 2026.11.1–2026.11.3 should note that post-install Doctor WAL publication verification can leave an update "partially finalized" (#197083).

Assessment: This is a corrective release, not a feature release. The rollback-safety work is directionally correct but does not yet resolve the broader class of migration/rollback interdependency bugs.

3. Project Progress

Merged/closed PRs (255 total in 24h). Notable closures and their impact:

  • #191324 [CLOSED] — improve(agents): name the child's runtime and credential on spawn receipts. This advanced spawn-receipt observability, exposing resolvedRuntime, resolvedAuth, and resolvedAuthProfile for primary models. Directly enabled follow-up test work (#200943).
  • #112313 [CLOSED] — Dead-lettered outbound delivery queue entries are permanent. A long-standing (since July) data-retention bug where failed delivery rows could never be read, retried, or cleared. Its closure removes a permanent health counter leak.
  • #158592 [CLOSED] — After host sleep/wake, prepared model runtime publication times out and never recovers. A P0 message-loss bug closed after ~7 weeks.
  • #158070 [CLOSED] — Preflight compaction fails with "agent tool caller authority is no longer active". A P1 message-loss bug affecting multi-agent deployments.
  • #191818, #187468, #137265, #153417, #155396, #138561 — A broad sweep of P1/P2 behavior, auth-provider, and memory bugs closed in this window.

Features advanced (still open but active):

  • #193550 — Plugin hook before_model_request to let plugins gate the final provider request (fail-closed policy hook). XL change, compatibility-flagged, awaiting author.
  • #196203 — Install local projects/templates through a live Gateway (openclaw templates add ./my-template).
  • #198455 — Allow plugins to contribute Prometheus metric families to the existing scrape route.
  • #141004 — Record observed runtime skill usage in the durable audit surface.

Observation: The project is closing older P1s effectively, but the incoming rate of new P1/P0 issues (see §5) roughly offsets it — net backlog is not shrinking.

4. Community Hot Topics

Ranked by comment count. Note that 👍 counts are strikingly low (0–4), indicating discussion is concentrated among a few highly engaged reporters.

Rank Item Comments Link
1 #164294 — Gateway state DB WAL auto-checkpoint never completes (blocked by in-process reader) 42 openclaw/openclaw#164294
2 #191944 — gateway stop / stop --force fail on macOS ("Process ancestry could not be fully inspected") 35 #191944
3 #150635 — Short-term recall retention evicts entries nightly; dreaming deep phase never promotes 29 #150635
4 #178359 — doctor --fix --non-interactive idles 15+ min, never reaches agent DB repair 26 #178359
5 #168955 — Startup regression 2026.10.1: ready ~1030s vs ~410s (Windows) 22 #168955
6 #197083 — Post-install Doctor WAL publication leaves 11.3 update partially finalized 21 #197083
7 #126360 — AgentSelectionRequiredError log flood under explicit multi-agent ownership 21 #126360
8 #48003 — Steer mode does not inject messages mid-turn for main sessions 20 (👍4) #48003

Underlying needs analysis:

  • Operational reliability of the state layer is the dominant theme: WAL checkpointing (#164294), update finalization (#197083), doctor repair hangs (#178359), and startup regressions (#168955) all point to SQLite/state-management fragility as the project's central stability risk.
  • Multi-agent deployments are a first-class use case (#126360, #48003, #155868, #194451) — users are running 6–7 agents with sessions_send routing and hitting coordination edge cases (turn claims, log floods, prompt-cache invalidation).
  • The "dreaming"/memory system is under scrutiny (#150635) — the deep-phase promotion pipeline silently stalls at cap, undermining a headline feature.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity (P0 > P1), with fix-PR status noted.

P0 (release blockers)

  • #161921 — After state-migrated-no-rollback, doctor --fix and plugins update each require the other; plugins stuck on previous release. No fix PR. (link)
  • #153426 — Curated memory roots (MEMORY.md/USER.md) silently and permanently excluded from bootstrap injection by the provenance ratchet; needs security review. No fix PR. (link)
  • #89278 — Codex OAuth refresh succeeds but cron/heartbeat fail with 10s auth refresh timeout. Linked PR open. (link)

P1 (crash / message-loss / data-loss)

  • #178359 — doctor --fix --non-interactive hangs 15+ min, never repairs agent DB (macOS). No fix PR. (link)
  • #168955 — Startup regression: sidecars.control-ui-assets blocks 477s on Windows. No fix PR. (link)
  • #185578 — Gateway heap floor only ratchets up; ~25 MiB/h leak until V8 cap aborts. Not repro on main. (link)
  • #181120 — macOS Gateway hangs with main thread blocked closing a worker MessagePort. Related PR #181551 open (disables auto-profiler to avoid native lock stall). (link)
  • #167406 — Windows MSIX: Codex-enabled Gateway startup starves main thread. No fix PR. (link)
  • #194403 — Helper-completion continuations invalidate their own authority; conversations blocked. No fix PR. (link)
  • #194451 — /think (and other directives) mid-turn kill the turn with SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError; #192585 only covered /status. Linked PR open. (link)
  • #157255 — Turn claim not released after lane timeout; session wedged 90+ min. No fix PR. (link)
  • #196505 — memory index --force aborts with "worker task capacity reached" instead of retrying on large corpora. No fix PR. (link)
  • #117262 — SQLite contention: 3 concurrent write handles cause ~33s event-loop stalls (DEF-61). No fix PR. (link)
  • #152965 — Hot-reloading a non-channel plugin disposes channel plugins without reconnecting; drops inbound messages. No fix PR. (link)
  • #166641 — web_fetch cold fallback synchronously captures unrelated plugins on main thread, causing liveness stalls. Linked PR open. (link)

P2 (notable)

  • #164294 (42 comments) — WAL auto-checkpoint never completes. No fix PR.
  • #197083 — Update partially finalized after WAL publication failure. No fix PR.
  • #182891 — Prompt cache never reused; cache read dropped N -> 0 on every request. No fix PR.
  • #192667 — macOS Settings slowness + dark-theme input visibility — reporter confirms both resolved on 2026.11.5. (link)

Fix-PR coverage note: Of the top-severity items, only a minority (#181120, #89278, #194451, #166641) have linked fix PRs. The most-commented and most-reproduced bugs (WAL checkpoint, doctor hang, state-migration deadlock) remain unfixed with no PR, which is the project's clearest health risk.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Request Issue Likelihood in next release
Mandatory Memory/Embedding setup in onboarding wizard #16670 Medium — low complexity, addresses a known adoption gap; P3 but widely felt
Enforceable checkpoints / bounded yields for long WebChat runs #138990 Medium — needs product decision, tied to foreground-run UX
Context budget / skip policy for Skill Workshop on oversized sessions #150238 Low-Medium — linked PR open, awaiting product decision
Plugin hook to gate final model provider request (before_model_request) PR #193550 Medium — XL PR active, but compatibility-flagged and awaiting author
Install local templates via live Gateway PR #196203 Medium — closes a concrete authoring gap
Plugin-contributed Prometheus metric families PR #198455 Medium — operational observability demand

Prediction: The next minor release is most likely to ship operational/observability improvements (Prometheus plugin metrics, template installation, spawn-receipt naming) rather than the higher-effort product decisions (checkpoint enforcement, memory onboarding). The memory/embedding onboarding step is the most likely user-facing addition because it is low-risk and addresses a documented setup failure.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points (ranked by frequency/severity):

  1. Updates break installations. Multiple reporters describe updates that fail at package-swap, leave state "partially finalized," or deadlock repair (#197083, #161921, #183479, #187468, #200756). One Windows user (#200756) hit a baseline package scan failure on beta.2→beta.4. This is the single most damaging theme for user trust.
  2. Startup and runtime performance regressions. #168955 (Windows startup 2.5× slower), #185578 (memory leak), #117262 (33s event-loop stalls) — users are measuring and reporting precisely, indicating production deployments under real load.
  3. Multi-agent coordination failures. Log floods, turn-claim wedges, prompt-cache misses, and duplicate messages (#126360, #48003, #157255, #39476, #155868).
  4. Memory system unreliability. Recall eviction (#150635), indexing failures (#196505), and silent memory-root exclusion (#153426) undercut a headline feature.

Satisfaction signals:

  • Users are highly engaged and technically capable — detailed repros, V8 profiles, symbolized samples. This is a committed, self-hosting audience.
  • #192667's reporter confirming resolution on 2026.11.5 shows fixes do land and are acknowledged.
  • Low 👍 counts suggest a small but deep community rather than a broad one; there is little "casual" feedback noise.

Dissatisfaction signals:

  • Repeated "still reproduces on current main" updates on long-lived issues (e.g., #167609, #141474) indicate maintainer response latency relative to reporter effort.
  • The state-migrated-no-rollback pattern is a recurring source of frustration because it removes the user's escape hatch.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-unanswered or high-impact items needing maintainer attention (all open, no fix PR unless noted):

Issue Age Why it needs attention
#48003 — Steer mode does not inject mid-turn Since 2026-03-16 (~8 mo) P1 session-state/message-loss; highest 👍 (4) on the board; core UX feature
#89278 — Codex OAuth cron/heartbeat 10s timeout Since 2026-06-02 (~5.5 mo) P0; linked PR open but stalled
#117262 — SQLite 3-handle contention (DEF-61) Since 2026-08-01 (~3.5 mo) P1 crash-loop; root-cause of many stall reports
#126360 — AgentSelectionRequiredError log flood Since 2026-08-19 (~3 mo) P2 but 21 comments; explicit multi-agent config
#153426 — Memory roots silently excluded (provenance ratchet) Since 2026-09-20 (~2 mo) P0, needs security review; data-loss for memory feature
#161921 — doctor/plugins mutual dependency after no-rollback Since 2026-09-30 (~7 wk) P0 release blocker; no PR
#164294 — WAL auto-checkpoint never completes Since 2026-10-03 (~6 wk) Most-commented issue (42); no fix PR
#178359 — doctor --fix hangs 15+ min Since 2026-10-20 (~4 wk) P1 crash-loop; blocks recovery from other bugs
PR #193550 — before_model_request plugin hook Since 2026-11-05 XL, compatibility risk, awaiting author — a key extensibility decision

Assessment: The project's health is mixed but not alarming. Maintainers are closing real P1s and shipping corrective releases, but the unfixed, high-comment cluster around state/SQLite/update machinery is aging past the point where reporters expect resolution. The most impactful single action would be a maintainer-owned state-layer hardening epic (WAL checkpointing, rollback semantics, doctor repair) — it would resolve or unblock roughly a third of the top-severity backlog simultaneously. Secondary priority: unblocking the P0 items #89278 and #153426, both of which have stalled despite clear reproductions.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — Personal AI Assistant / Agent OSS Ecosystem

Snapshot: 2026-11-18 | Projects: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw

1. Ecosystem Overview

The agent/personal-AI-assistant OSS landscape is past the feature-race phase and into a hardening phase. Every project except IronClaw is processing high issue/PR volumes (>20 issues touched/24h), yet all five share the same bottleneck: a growing backlog of state-layer, session-lifecycle, and update-machinery defects that cap production reliability. The community is small, technically deep, and self-hosting — evidenced by low 👍 counts (0–4) alongside detailed V8 profiles, SQLite WAL traces, and symbolized stack samples. Security boundaries (approval gating, emergency stop, hook fail-open behavior) have emerged as a cross-cutting concern, driven by auditors rather than casual users. Meanwhile, plugin architecture has become the universal roadmap bet: four of five projects are actively extracting capabilities (MCP, memory, local models, channels, theming) into plugin surfaces.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Issues (24h) PRs (24h) Release Status Net Backlog Trend Health Score
OpenClaw 472 touched (361 open / 111 closed) 500 touched (245 open / 255 merged) v2026.11.5 shipped (stability patch) ⚠️ Flat — intake ≈ closure 6.5/10
Hermes Agent 50 updated (50 open / 0 closed) 50 touched (42 open / 8 merged) v0.23.2 canary (no changelog) 🔴 Growing — no closures 4.5/10
IronClaw 0 updated 10 touched (all Dependabot) None 🟡 Stalled — automated only 3.5/10
QwenPaw 23 updated (11 open / 12 closed) 50 touched (29 open / 21 merged) None (post-2.3.0 stabilization) 🟢 Healthy churn 7.5/10
ZeroClaw 21 touched (all open) 50 touched (41 open / 9 merged) v0.9.1 in preparation 🟡 Stabilizing 6/10

Scoring basis: closure ratio, presence of fix PRs for top-severity bugs, release cadence, community engagement depth, and backlog age for P0/S0 items.

Notes:

  • OpenClaw's absolute numbers dwarf peers (~10× Hermes/ZeroClaw), but its fix-PR coverage on top-severity bugs is the weakest in relative terms — the most-commented issues (WAL checkpoint #164294, doctor hang #178359) have zero PRs.
  • Hermes Agent's 50-open/0-closed issue day is the single clearest red flag in the dataset.
  • QwenPaw is the only project with same-day fix turnaround on a high-severity bug (#8700 → #8701) and a healthy open/closed PR ratio (~1.4:1).

3. OpenClaw's Position

Advantages vs. peers:

  • Reference implementation status. OpenClaw ships the most capabilities in-flight (plugin hooks before_model_request, live template install, Prometheus plugin metrics, spawn-receipt observability) and is the only project with a formal compatibility-flagged change process.
  • Largest observed community footprint — 472 issues + 500 PRs in 24h vs. Hermes' 50+50, ZeroClaw's 21+50, QwenPaw's 23+50, IronClaw's 0+10. This is roughly 5–45× the throughput of any peer.
  • Most mature release discipline — v2026.11.5 demonstrates a corrective-release cadence peers lack (Hermes ships canary with no changelog; IronClaw has no release; QwenPaw/ZeroClaw are mid-cycle).

Technical approach differences:

  • Deep investment in SQLite/WAL as the durable substrate with an in-process reader model — this is the source of both OpenClaw's durability and its worst bottleneck (auto-checkpoint never completes, 3-handle contention causing 33s event-loop stalls).
  • Multi-agent is first-class — sessions_send routing, turn claims, lane timeouts, prompt-cache invalidation are native concerns. Peers treat multi-agent as an extension (Hermes' A2A RFC #132248; QwenPaw's subagent batch dispatch).
  • "Dreaming"/memory as a headline feature with a deep-phase promotion pipeline — Hermes and ZeroClaw have memory backends (ReMeLight, Lucid) but neither ships an equivalent autonomous memory-consolidation loop.

Community size comparison:

  • OpenClaw: deep, technically sophisticated, low casual noise → narrow but committed.
  • QwenPaw: broadest channel surface (WeChat, DingTalk, Telegram, Feishu, QQ) → widest geographic/user diversity.
  • Hermes/ZeroClaw: migration-driven (moltis migrants reference parity) with strong contributor momentum.
  • IronClaw: no visible community activity in the window.

Weakness: OpenClaw's ratio of reported severity to fix-PR coverage is the worst of the five. #161921 (P0 state-migration deadlock, open 7 weeks, no PR) and #153426 (P0 memory-root silent exclusion, needs security review) are trust-critical and unowned.

4. Shared Technical Focus Areas

These requirements appear independently across ≥3 projects — strong signals of ecosystem-wide maturity gaps:

Focus Area Projects Specific Needs
Plugin architecture as extension surface OpenClaw (#193550 hooks), Hermes (#132248 A2A plugin), QwenPaw (#8554 CLI, #8469 MCP, #8499 local-models, #8071 theming), ZeroClaw (#12449 MCP OAuth) Stable semantic contracts (theming tokens, tool hooks, capability gating); MCP extraction into first-class plugin
Session/admission state durability OpenClaw (#157255 turn-claim wedge, #194451 transcript conflict), Hermes (#157169 FIFO wedge, #148540 restore_policy, #150056 admission_conflict), ZeroClaw (#9191 cron lock), QwenPaw (#8771 DingTalk collision) Persisted state must round-trip; stale admission records must self-heal after restart; permanent wedges are the worst failure class
Security/approval enforcement gaps Hermes (#59293 CLI bypass, #100942 hook fail-open, #156884 symlink write), ZeroClaw (#9390/#9802 emergency stop, #12514 supervised SOP bypass, #7821 sandbox policy), OpenClaw (#153426 provenance ratchet) Uniform enforcement across all entry points; fail-closed defaults; auditable boundaries
Cost/quota/config semantics honesty ZeroClaw (#12477 enforcement mode ignored), QwenPaw (#8776 misclassification, #8798 quota error UX), OpenClaw (context budget #150238), Hermes (tool budgets #80508) Config knobs must do what they say; graceful fallback on quota exhaustion
Channel/integration reliability QwenPaw (WeChat #8709/#8693, DingTalk #8771), Hermes (WhatsApp #63647, Discord #121938), ZeroClaw (VoiceHost #9740, Telegram reasoning #11744) Release QA for channel plugins; per-channel session isolation invariants
Observability for ops OpenClaw (Prometheus metrics #198455, spawn receipts #191324), Hermes (#11116 latency metadata), ZeroClaw (#12476 gateway log flood), IronClaw (latency harness via wasmtime/rustls bumps) Per-tool/per-request metrics; sensible log levels

Convergent need: Agents need a durable, self-healing session substrate. Four of five projects report permanent-wedge bugs from persisted state that their own writers produce but their readers reject.

5. Differentiation Analysis

Dimension OpenClaw Hermes Agent QwenPaw ZeroClaw IronClaw
Primary focus Reference multi-agent runtime Desktop + A2A collaboration Multi-channel / plugin marketplace Safety-enforced production runtime Latency/perf harness
Target users Power users, multi-agent operators Desktop-first individual + small teams CJK enterprise + broad consumer channels Security-conscious operators Perf engineers (internal)
Distinctive tech SQLite/WAL, dreaming memory, spawn receipts 6-PR desktop profile-routing stack, A2A transport WeChat/DingTalk/Feishu adapters, plugin catalog Emergency-stop enforcement, sandbox policy, SOP engine Rust product crates + WASM runtime
Architecture posture Monolithic core with plugin hooks Desktop app + gateway + plugin catalog Gateway + channel plugins + console Gateway + channels + SOP + memory backends Rust harness-first
Where it's strong Capability breadth, observability Desktop perf iteration Channel diversity, localization (BiDi, CJK) Safety posture, security audits Low-level runtime work
Where it's weak State-layer hardening; fix-PR coverage Session durability; issue closure rate Release-QA for new channels; durable persistence trust Fix-PR velocity on S1s Community activity; human-authored progress

Key architectural split: OpenClaw/Hermes/ZeroClaw own the gateway + persistent-state pattern with different optimization targets (breadth / desktop UX / safety). QwenPaw optimizes for channel reach with a shallower per-adapter isolation model — which is why cross-user session collision (#8771) is uniquely a QwenPaw-class bug. IronClaw is an outlier: a perf-harness project rather than a product runtime.

6. Community Momentum & Maturity

Activity tiers:

  • Tier 1 — High-velocity, strained: OpenClaw (~1,000 events/24h). Iterating fastest, but intake ≈ closure → net backlog flat. Rapidly iterating, not stabilizing.
  • Tier 2 — High-velocity, healthier: QwenPaw (~73 events, 12 issues closed, 21 PRs merged). Rapidly iterating with real churn — the most balanced project. ZeroClaw (~71 events, 9 PRs closed) is close but closure-starved on S1s.
  • Tier 3 — Moderate velocity, stalling: Hermes Agent (~100 events, 0 issues closed). Iterating in PR count but not converging. Risk of reporter fatigue.
  • Tier 4 — Low/automated: IronClaw (10 Dependabot PRs, 0 human activity). Maintainer-review-lag phase.

Maturity signals:

  • Most mature process: OpenClaw (compatibility-flagged PRs, corrective releases).
  • Most mature safety posture: ZeroClaw (S0/S1 triage discipline, RUSTSEC tracking, sandbox RFC).
  • Most mature release-velocity on features: QwenPaw (same-day fix PRs, plugin marketplace shipping).
  • Least mature continuity: Hermes (canary release with no changelog; critical security issue #59293 open 4.5 months with needs-decision).

Contributor health: QwenPaw and ZeroClaw both received same-day fixes from first-time or external contributors (#8701, #11598) — a healthy signal. OpenClaw's author concentration (e.g., @steipete on the release) suggests bus-factor risk. IronClaw shows zero contributor signal.

7. Trend Signals

For AI agent developers and platform decision-makers:

  1. The state layer is the product. SQLite/WAL contention (OpenClaw #117262, #164294), session FIFOs (Hermes #157169), cron locks (ZeroClaw #9191), and admission conflicts (Hermes #150056) all point to the same conclusion: durable session state with self-healing reconciliation is now the differentiator, not model choice or tool count. Buyers should evaluate agent frameworks on their failure modes after restart, mid-turn interruption, and profile switch — not on demo polish.

  2. Security controls are failing open by default. Three independent projects report approval/emergency/hook controls that silently do nothing in production deployments (Hermes #100942 under systemd, ZeroClaw #9390 runtime emergency stop, OpenClaw #153426 memory provenance). Fail-closed must be the default; audit each entry point. Expect enterprise RFPs to demand this within 2–3 release cycles.

  3. Plugin extensibility is the new moat — and the new attack surface. Four of five projects are extracting subsystems into plugins. The downstream need is a stable semantic contract: theming tokens (QwenPaw #8071), pre-request hooks (OpenClaw #193550), OAuth for remote MCP (ZeroClaw #12449). New plugins must be able to gate — not just decorate — the request path.

  4. Channel breadth is a QA liability. QwenPaw's WeChat ACCOUNT_IN_USE duplicate reports (#8709, #8693) and DingTalk session collision (#8771) show that shipping many channels without per-adapter isolation invariants creates silent cross-user data mixing. Channel plugins need conformance tests before release.

  5. Configuration semantics must be honest. ZeroClaw's cost.enforcement.mode: "warn" that still stops turns (#12477), QwenPaw's quota-error misclassification (#8776), and OpenClaw's context-budget gaps (#150238) all erode operator trust. A config flag that doesn't do what it says is worse than no flag.

  6. The memory feature is a trust surface, not a novelty. OpenClaw's stalling deep-phase promotion (#150635), silent memory-root exclusion (#153426), and QwenPaw's ReMeLight cost concerns (#7719) reveal that "autonomous memory" is not production-ready in any project today. Treat memory pipelines as security-sensitive data paths, not UX flourishes.

  7. Observability is becoming table-stakes for ops. Prometheus plugin metrics (OpenClaw), per-tool latency reporting (Hermes #11116), and log-level control (ZeroClaw #12476) are being requested by self-hosting operators — signaling that agents are entering the "boring infrastructure" phase where SRE tooling matters more than capability headlines.

Bottom line for developers choosing a framework: QwenPaw currently offers the best forward-momentum/closure ratio; OpenClaw offers the richest capability surface at the cost of state-layer debt; ZeroClaw is the best fit for security-sensitive deployments; Hermes Agent needs to demonstrate issue-closure velocity before it can be recommended for production; IronClaw is not a candidate for external adoption at this time.

  • #8771 [OPEN] DingTalk session collision — security-adjacent (cross-user session mixing) and has no linked fix PR; should be prioritized above cosmetic issues. Link

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-18

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw remains in a high-activity, pre-release stabilization phase: 21 issues were touched in the last 24h (all still open/active) and 50 PRs were updated, with 9 merged/closed and 41 still open. No new releases were published, but the volume of release:v0.9.1-tagged work (Lucid backend retirement, dependency security fixes, Windows test triage) indicates the v0.9.1 milestone is actively being assembled. The day's activity skews heavily toward bug triage and security hardening — multiple S0/S1 issues were touched, including an emergency-stop enforcement gap and a supervised-SOP approval bypass — suggesting the project is prioritizing correctness and safety over new features right now. Overall health is strong on throughput but strained on stability: several long-lived, high-risk issues remain open with no fix PRs yet.

2. Releases

None. No new releases were published in the last 24h. (Note: several PRs and issues are tagged release:v0.9.1, indicating v0.9.1 is in preparation but not yet cut.)

3. Project Progress

Merged/closed PRs today (9 total; notable items):

  • #9740 [CLOSED] — feat(channels): add VoiceHost WebSocket bridge. A large opt-in bridge allowing external FunASR/SenseVoice audio hosts to exchange transcripts, replies, interruption, and approval events with ZeroClaw. This is a significant voice-channel capability landing after months in the parking lot.
  • #9229 [CLOSED] — fix(runtime): make interactive Ctrl+C state-aware. Reworks the REPL's signal handling into a single persistent Idle/Active/Stopping lifecycle, replacing per-turn listeners. A long-running (July) fix that improves interactive reliability.
  • #11238 [CLOSED] — fix(config): accept tagged declarative cron schedules. Fixes #11237; config PATCH/PUT and /config/cron now correctly save tagged cron schedule objects.
  • #11647 [CLOSED] — fix(providers): decouple vision support from system merge. Corrects a gating bug where image-part support was incorrectly tied to system-prompt merging.
  • #11598 [CLOSED] — feat(security): support glob matching in the command allowlist. Lets operators allow directory trees (e.g., skill/plugin script folders) instead of enumerating every file.
  • #11779 / #11780 [CLOSED] — SOP tooling fixes: sop list now surfaces malformed SOP.toml failures and exits non-zero; max_concurrent_total is documented and named in capacity refusals.

In-flight notable PRs (open): #12521 (retire Lucid memory backend), #12449 (generic OAuth 2.1 + PKCE for remote MCP servers), #11744 (stream reasoning in Telegram/Slack drafts), #12516 (dependency security fixes).

4. Community Hot Topics

  • #8600 — Per-chat model switching for multi-model providers (5 comments, 1 👍, open since July). A moltis migrant requests easy switching between any model a provider supports. Underlying need: users want provider-level model catalogs (e.g., OpenRouter's full set) exposed per conversation without reconfiguring the agent. Tagged status:parking-lot and risk:high — a design-heavy request.

  • #12401 — Tool-context collapse breaks Claude Opus 5.5 chats (5 comments, S1). Once an older tool-using turn leaves the keep_tool_context_turns window, every subsequent request fails with a thinking-signature 400. Underlying need: correct interaction between context-window pruning and Anthropic's signed-thinking contract.

  • #9191 — Cron agent jobs have no wall-clock timeout (5 comments, P1, S1). In-flight locks are only cleared at process start; a hung agent job can block indefinitely. Underlying need: production-grade scheduler isolation and cancellation budgets.

  • #9644 — Retire the Lucid memory backend (4 comments, updated today). Lucid wraps SQLite but shells out to an external lucid command on every store/recall. The corresponding PR #12521 is now open, making this a likely v0.9.1 deliverable.

  • #9390 / #9802 — Emergency stop is CLI-only; RFC for full enforcement (4 and 3 comments, P1, risk:high). A security audit found the emergency-stop state file is never read by runtime paths. The RFC proposes interrupting in-flight tool work and enforcing network-kill/domain-block at the shared egress boundary. This is the most consequential safety gap in the tracker.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity:

  • S0 — #12514: Supervised SOP skips approval when step 1's decide question is answered "no." The engine skips step 1 before its approval gate, so a supervised SOP asks for no approval at all. Data-loss/security risk. No fix PR referenced yet.
  • S1 — #12401: Claude Opus 5.5 thinking-signature 400 after tool-context collapse. Workflow-blocking regression since v0.9.0. A related fix exists for a different symptom: PR #12509 stops replaying unsigned thinking blocks (fixes #12504), but the collapse-window interaction itself appears unfixed.
  • S1 — #9191: Cron agent jobs lack wall-clock timeout. No fix PR.
  • S1 — #12477: cost.enforcement.mode is ignored. An exceeded budget always stops the turn even in the default "warn" mode. No fix PR.
  • S1 — #9390: Emergency stop not enforced at runtime. RFC #9802 tracks the fix; a first enforcement slice landed via PR #9440 (per issue text), but full coverage is pending.
  • S2 — #12504: Anthropic provider replays unsigned thinking blocks. Fix PR #12509 is open.
  • S2 — #12492: Dashboard chats ignore runtime-profile thinking settings. No native thinking config is ever sent from the web dashboard. No fix PR.
  • S2 — #12476: Gateway logs every connection at INFO, flooding runtime traces. No fix PR.
  • S2 — #12489: Cron scheduler waits for the whole due batch, so one long agent job delays all others. No fix PR.
  • S3 — #12507: Web chat shows [CURRENT DATE & TIME: …] prefix and synthetic timestamps after reload. Fix PR #12515 is open.

Also of note: #12505 tracks replacement of unmaintained chrono/chrono-tz (RUSTSEC-2026-0543/0555), which currently fails the Security CI job on every build; PR #12516 updates zip for RUSTSEC-2026-0548 and accepts the chrono advisories as a stopgap.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • Per-chat model switching (#8600) — high user interest, but parked and high-risk; unlikely before v0.9.1.
  • Runtime-profile thinking levels for OpenAI (#12054) and the dashboard counterpart (#12492) — consistent thinking-level plumbing across providers and surfaces. A natural v0.9.1/v0.10 candidate given the adjacent Anthropic thinking fixes already in flight.
  • Scoped operator-managed service credentials (#12422) — an RFC for authorizing agents against services without exposing the underlying credential to the model or chat. Security-model change; likely to mature over multiple releases.
  • Complete emergency-stop enforcement (#9802) — an RFC with a partial implementation already merged; expect incremental slices in v0.9.1+.
  • Lucid memory backend retirement (#9644) — PR #12521 is open and tagged release:v0.9.1; strong candidate for the next release (breaking: configs selecting Lucid migrate to SQLite).
  • Generic MCP OAuth 2.1 + PKCE (#12449) — large XL PR enabling authenticated remote MCP servers; a notable capability expansion if it lands.

Prediction: v0.9.1 will most likely bundle the Lucid retirement, the zip security bump, the SOP/dashboard fixes already in PR, and possibly the Anthropic unsigned-thinking fix. Larger items (OAuth MCP, voice bridge follow-ups, thinking-level parity) look like v0.10 material.

7. User Feedback Summary

Real users are hitting provider-integration friction more than anything else: the Anthropic thinking-signature class of bugs (#12401, #12504) blocks Claude Opus 5.5 users after a few tool turns, and dashboard users report their configured thinking settings are silently ignored (#12492). A moltis migrant (#8600) explicitly praises ZeroClaw's capability parity but flags per-chat model switching as the one missing convenience — a satisfaction signal with a clear gap. Production operators are voicing scheduler and cost-control reliability concerns: cron jobs with no timeout (#9191), batch-serialized cron execution (#12489), and a cost-enforcement mode that doesn't actually warn (#12477). Security-minded users and auditors are driving the emergency-stop thread (#9390/#9802) and the supervised-SOP approval bypass (#12514) — the latter is the most alarming report of the day. Minor but recurring UX papercuts appear in the web dashboard (#12507). Overall sentiment: the feature set is valued, but users are asking for predictable failure modes and honest configuration semantics before adding more surface area.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-unanswered or under-attended items that deserve maintainer attention:

  • #8600 (open since 2026-07-01, parking-lot) — per-chat model switching; four months old with only 5 comments and one 👍. Needs a design decision or explicit deferral.
  • #9191 (open since 2026-07-20, P1/S1) — cron job timeout; nearly four months without a fix PR despite workflow-blocking severity.
  • #9390 (open since 2026-07-26) and #9802 (open since 2026-08-07) — emergency-stop enforcement; partial progress via #9440 but the RFC remains open and high-risk.
  • #9644 (open since 2026-08-01) — Lucid retirement; now has an open PR (#12521), so it is moving, but the issue itself has sat for 3.5 months.
  • #7821 (open since 2026-06-17, XL, risk:high) — canonical sandbox_policy schema with application-layer enforcement; five months open and a foundational security change that likely needs reviewer bandwidth.
  • #12449 (XL, MCP OAuth) — recently active but very large; at risk of review fatigue.

Health note: Throughput is healthy (9 PRs closed, active triage), but the concentration of S0/S1 issues without fix PRs (#12514, #9191, #12477, #12489) and the five-month-old security PR #7821 are the main risks to the v0.9.1 timeline. The Lucid retirement and dependency-security work are the clearest, best-scoped wins to close first.
