  4. #52894 — Show exact free usage limit reset time (13 comments, 👍8) — Directly complements #59387. Users want a real timestamp instead of "reset at ..." with no actual reset. Low-effort, high-trust value.

  5. #54371 — [reproduced] ACP: slash commands execute but never stream output (9 comments, 👍6) — Reproduced bug in JetBrains Rider ACP sessions: commands run but the chat shows nothing. Breaks the IDE integration story for a growing user segment.

  6. #62529 — ChatGPT subscription-sharing limit error despite available allowance (9 comments) — macOS 2.2.5 rejects a simple "Hello" with subscription_sharing_usage_limit_exceeded while the ChatGPT usage page shows 89% remaining. Classic quota-sync mismatch.

  7. #64085 — NAND/SSD drives failing under heavy local load in Russian (8 comments) — Severe hardware-level report: two machines' M.2 drives failing while running local models under max load. Triaged as type/bug, platform/windows. Warrants urgent investigation whether it's thermal/IO saturation or unrelated.

  8. #64084 — Independent Java 25 benchmark: strengths, weaknesses, roadmap (7 comments) — A community-authored engineering-quality benchmark against OpenCode V2 with a proposed roadmap. Valuable outside-in signal on performance positioning.

  9. #56386 — cli: run resolves workspace from $PWD instead of process cwd (6 comments) — Confirmed on 2.0.32 and still relevant in v2 paths. Breaks containers, systemd units, and any subprocess spawner — a correctness bug with wide blast radius.

  10. #64121 — Model bypasses Plan mode file-write restrictions via shell heredocs (3 comments) — Security-relevant: an agent in Plan mode wrote files by using shell heredocs, circumventing the permission model. Small comment count, but this is the kind of report that should escalate fast.

Also worth watching: #63892 (Store PowerShell spawn 0xC0070005 on 2.3.0), #63976 (PTY daemon zombie leak), #64117 (tools/list_changed not surfacing new MCP tools).

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #63412 — fix(mcp): propagate tool-call trace context — Passes traceparent/tracestate through MCP calls. Observability win for anyone debugging multi-hop agent flows; partial implementation of #46856.

  2. #64140 — feat(server): async video generation API with disk-backed media — The HTTP half of the media plan, pairing with the agent-tool PR #63666. Signals OpenCode moving into generative media tooling.

  3. #62490 — feat(tui): choose export destination in the new export dialog — Adds a Location picker to /export, building on #62253. Quality-of-life for TUI session archival.

  4. #64139 — feat(app): name a paired server from its QR code — QR pairing payloads can now carry a display name; manual naming and later renames still work. Smooths mobile/remote pairing UX.

  5. #64137 — fix(service): retry Windows pipe spawn on packaged access denied (closes #63892) — Direct fix for the Microsoft Store PowerShell 7 spawn failure. High-priority Windows unblock; tagged needs:compliance.

  6. #63542 — fix(ssh): recover when the remote service port is taken (closes #54059) — Makes SSH reconnects resilient when the port is already bound post-drop. Fixes a confusing "Could not establish the SSH connection" failure mode.

  7. #64133 — fix(core): retry incomplete Claude context discovery after cooldown — Follow-up to #64107 addressing #61020: Claude Agent catalogs cap context at 200K instead of 1M, causing premature compaction. Big impact on long-context Claude Code users.

  8. #64126 — fix(cli): use actual cwd instead of stale $PWD — Fixes the run/mini cwd bug (related to #56386) and adds regression tests plus a TUI fallback fix. Complemented by #64128 for the full TUI path.

  9. #64134 — feat(server): preview Slack links through OpenCode Console — New experimental endpoint behind a console_slack_preview flag. First concrete step toward Slack-as-a-surface workflow.

  10. #55847 — fix(core): missing session directory now a typed, actionable error — Kills the silent-failure mode where a moved/deleted project folder produces an empty turn. Part of the automated cleanup batch, but a legitimately good DX fix.

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided for this window.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Billing & entitlement transparency — Exact reset timestamps (#52894), crypto payment support (#23153, 69 👍), and rationalized quota errors (#62529, #59387) dominate by engagement. Users want to see and control what they're paying for.
  • Permission and sandboxing rigor — Better execution permissions (#48411), Plan mode enforcement after the heredoc bypass (#64121), and whitelisting plugin tools by name (#64051). The permission model is being stress-tested and found porous at the edges.
  • Agent lifecycle control — Stop background subagents from the web app (#52016), foreground subagent execution restored (#64073), accurate Subagents tab status (#62365). Background execution is confusing users and the UI doesn't compensate.
  • UX polish for long sessions — Image attachments from tool results in chat (#21227, 13 👍), stable timeline scrolling (#56130), thicker scrollbar (#64064), Windows taskbar badge counts (#62042).
  • Platform-specific coverage — smolvm/smolmachine support (#64112), Store PowerShell fixes (#63892), path handling for Ollama on Windows (#54890).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Windows is the least stable platform right now. PowerShell spawn failures (0xC0070005), zombie PTY processes under v2.3.0, backslash-stripping in MCP arguments with Ollama, and stale $PWD resolution all concentrate on Windows. Several fixes are in flight (#64137, #64126/#64128), but v2.3.0's Windows experience is rough.
  • Quota and entitlement errors are the top community grievance. Between the 370-comment free-tier thread and the paid-tier region bug (#50155), the gap between what the server enforces and what the UI communicates is the single biggest source of frustration — and the highest-leverage fix.
  • Silent failures and mismatched state. Missing directories that produce empty turns (#55847), free-tier resets that never happen, and "inactive" subagents that are actually waiting (#62365). Users consistently describe the same failure shape: the app says nothing is wrong while nothing works.
  • Under-observed integration layers. MCP tool-list changes not reaching the model (#64117), ACP slash-command output vanishing (#54371), and Claude Agent context windows capped at 200K (#61020). The protocol edges (ACP, MCP, provider catalogs) need stronger test coverage.
  • Security model edge cases. The Plan-mode heredoc bypass (#64121) plus the plugin-tool whitelisting gap (#64051) suggest the permission system's resource/action model isn't being exercised against adversarial-but-plausible agent behavior.
Pi — earendil-works/pi

Pi Community Digest — 2026-11-16

1. Today's Highlights

No new releases landed in the last 24 hours, but issue activity was heavy: a burst of untriaged bug reports around session/model resolution, MCP status visibility, and docs site breakage. The standout P0 is a concurrency bug (#11950) where bash and read tool calls in the same assistant message execute in parallel, breaking sequential assumptions. Meanwhile, the ACP discussion continues to accumulate traction (54 👍) as the community pushes for editor interoperability beyond Pi's custom RPC dialect.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #11950 [OPEN] [bug, prio:p0] Tool calls run concurrently — read races bash — The most severe open issue: same-message bash + read start simultaneously, so reads hit stale/not-yet-written files. P0 with 7 comments. Link
  2. #11021 [OPEN] ChatGPT sign-in reports 272K context for GPT-6.1 Sol despite 500K catalog — Auth-path regression shrinks context/compaction budget vs. server-advertised limit. 14 comments, 8 👍 — the most-engaged open issue. Link
  3. #8810 [OPEN] Extension providers intermittently ignored for defaultProvider/defaultModel — Fresh sessions silently fall back to another provider's default; longstanding since August, 11 comments. Link
  4. #12076 [OPEN] Compaction: tool loop ends silently instead of compacting — At context limit, Pi exits the loop with no compaction rather than recovering; reproduced twice on 1.5.2 + vLLM. Link
  5. #9448 [OPEN] pi auth check blind to extension-registered providers — Breaks scripted/CI gating (reports invalid_state); blocks non-interactive pipelines. Link
  6. #12185 [CLOSED] Gemini model switch mid-task → 400 "Invalid thought signature" — Mid-session model switch after tool execution breaks OpenAI-compatible replay; affects LiteLLM/proxy users. Link
  7. #12187 [CLOSED] Session restore silently switches models when provider rewrites IDs — Resumed session ran on xai/grok-4.7 instead of default, rebuilding an 80k-token cache for $0.16 without warning. Link
  8. #12186 [CLOSED] Two prompts to idle session both start a run (regression in 1.5.1) — Second call rejects with "Agent is already running"; concurrency regression. Link
  9. #12184 [CLOSED] Google adapters reject Gemini 4 Hydrogen xhigh thinking level — Advertised thinking level throws before any HTTP request is sent. Link
  10. #12194 [CLOSED] Intermittent 400 from Cloudflare Workers AI connector — Content-shape validation mismatch on messages[0].content (array vs. required). Link

Also worth noting: #11226 (codemode script fails when declaring a top-level tools variable), #12190 (flaky AuthStorage coalesced-reload test, 8/20 pass on current main), and #12183 (Windows terminal escape-sequence leak when Node.js is updated mid-session).

4. Key PR Progress

Only one PR was updated in the window:

  1. #11854 [OPEN] fix(coding-agent): kill whole process trees of bash commands on Windows — taskkill /F /T misses descendants whose parent already exited; this fix targets orphaned background processes (e.g. (while true; do echo tick; done) &). Link

No other PRs were updated in the last 24 hours. The repository is currently issue-heavy and PR-light — worth watching if the backlog of untriaged bugs continues to grow.

5. Hot Discussions

Ideas

  • #4444 [General] Supporting the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) — Proposal to adopt ACP so any ACP-speaking editor can integrate without a bespoke client for Pi's RPC dialect. Strongest signal of intent in the tracker: 54 👍, 5 comments. Link

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Standardized editor integration — ACP support (#4444) is the clearest demand: stop requiring per-editor clients for Pi's proprietary RPC.
  • MCP observability — A cluster of requests (#10871, #12074, #12189) to publish native MCP connection status via ctx.ui.setStatus for custom footers; plus #12188 to embed Pi session IDs in MCP tools/call metadata for server-side correlation.
  • Durable cancellation semantics — #12090 requests cancellation handlers that can await signals/deadlines and checkpoint before exit.
  • TUI quality-of-life — #12182 asks for a full-text preview pane under /tree so long entries can be read in place.
  • Custom model typing — #12140 requests declaring non-chat (classifier) models via models.json.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Session/model resolution is fragile. Extension-registered providers intermittently ignored (#8810), provider key renames strand sessions (#12193), provider ID rewrites silently switch models on restore (#12187), and auth check can't see extension providers (#9448). This cluster is the single largest source of frustration.
  • Concurrency correctness. Parallel tool calls violating ordering (#11950) and double-run races on idle sessions (#12186) suggest the run scheduler needs hardening.
  • Context/compaction reliability. Mismatched context windows (#11021) and silent loop termination at the limit instead of compaction (#12076) directly cost tokens and break long tasks.
  • Provider adapter edge cases. Gemini thinking-level rejection (#12184), thought-signature failures on model switch (#12185), Cloudflare Workers AI 400s (#12194), and codex WebSocket errors masked by HTTP fallback (#12191).
  • Docs site brokenness. #12173 and #12192 report /latest/latest/... double-prefixed links returning 404 across article bodies — a quick win with visible community impact.
  • Windows ergonomics. Terminal escape-sequence leakage on mid-session Node.js updates (#12183) and incomplete process-tree cleanup (#11854).
  • Test flakiness as a signal. #12190's AuthStorage reload test failing 12/20 runs on main points to mtime-resolution assumptions that may mask real reload bugs.
Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code Community Digest — 2026-11-16

1. Today's Highlights

Managed Agent infrastructure dominates this cycle: the team landed the ability for Managed Agent sessions to access granted local directories and open interactive Managed Web Terminals without persisting credentials or paths (#16844). The v0.27.4 release bundles these changes alongside the TypeScript SDK v0.1.34, and the DingTalk adapter continues to expand Managed Agent's enterprise channel coverage. Meanwhile, the 1.0 Preview loop kernel migration (#17045) has closed, signaling the event-driven query() kernel is being progressively landed on main.

2. Releases

v0.27.4 (stable)

  • Registers client filesystems into managed sessions (#16844), enabling granted local directory access within Managed Agent sessions.
  • Enables interactive Managed Web Terminal access without persisting credentials or filesystem paths.

v0.27.3-nightly.20261115.6e3b2dcc19

  • feat(web-shell): sidebar workspace filter (#17244).
  • feat(managed-agent): DingTalk adapter added.

sdk-typescript-v0.1.34

  • Bundles CLI version 0.27.4, built from the same branch/ref as the SDK.

desktop-v0.27.4

  • Mirrors the managed-agent client filesystem registration and web-shell terminal test coverage.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #14724 — Main CI failed: Managed Agent gate — no test identified (383 comments). The single most-active issue in the repo. A persistent CI gate failure with no test attributed; sustained bot activity suggests an unresolved routing/attribution bug in the Managed Agent CI pipeline.

  2. #13078 — Daily dependency CVE audit failed (52 comments). Scheduled audit keeps failing; community is watching whether this is a genuine new vulnerability or an npm audit endpoint outage. Ties directly into #17099.

  3. #17045 — Land the 1.0 Preview loop kernel on main (18 comments, CLOSED). The tracking issue for migrating to an event-driven kernel behind a single query() entry point. Its closure marks a milestone in the 1.0 architecture.

  4. #14104 — Main CI failed: SDK Java HostedShellLifecycleRecoveryIT (17 comments). Hosted shell resource recovery under deletion is failing in the Java SDK, flagged ready-for-agent.

  5. #17099 — Track remaining npm security scan findings and staged dependency upgrades (14 comments). Snyk reported 29 findings across 43 dependency paths via @qwen-code/web-shell@0.26.3 and @qwen-code/sdk@0.1.25. Security-tagged and wide in scope.

  6. #16425 — Workflow agent permission approval never renders; run hangs (11 comments, CLOSED). A P1 core bug where the harness raised PermissionRequest and the status bar showed a pending badge, but no dialog rendered. Closure suggests a fix landed.

  7. #17332 — Auto mode: subagent batch renders only one approval dialog (3 comments). Parallel approval requests in a single batch orphan all but the last, freezing the batch. Directly related to the #16425 family of approval-rendering defects.

  8. #17380 — Managed Agent Turn fails with hosted_harness_unavailable during workspace provisioning (3 comments). Turns fail permanently after ~37s even though the runtime comes up shortly after — a race between provisioning and admission.

  9. #17381 — Managed hooks reject supported description/statusMessage metadata (3 comments). The managed hook manifest parser's closed key allowlist rejects standard metadata, blocking extension installs. Fix PR #17393 is already open.

  10. #17386 — CLI parallel-agent display sanitizes activity text but not agent name (3 comments). A security issue: the agent name passes through only the weaker ANSI-only filter, leaving an injection surface flagged by the project's own scanner.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #17228 — Codex-style managed worktree sessions (default-on, detached, branch & handoff). Web Shell sessions in trusted Git workspaces now default to isolated worktrees created lazily on first message, in detached HEAD for parallel safety. Phases P1–P5.

  2. #17378 — Add delivery-unit change overview for sessions. A new Web Shell right-panel tab rolling up changed files with +/- scale, segmented by delivery unit rather than conversation turn.

  3. #17377 — Track model availability for the fallback chain (Qoder port). Ports the Qoder preview line's per-model health ledger into main as a session-scoped state machine under the Option B integration decision.

  4. #17141 — Retain the latest complete operation during compaction. Keeps tool calls and results together verbatim post-compaction, summarizing only older history — addresses long-session fidelity.

  5. #17375 — Close the context trust refusal's root-tmp and hard-link bypasses. Hardens the verify-pr checker to fail closed and binds verification snapshots by content — a security-boundary fix.

  6. #16661 — Repair the MCP connection torn down by an aborted tool call. Aborting an in-flight MCP request used to leave the server DISCONNECTED; the abort path now arms transport repair.

  7. #15936 — Reduce or refuse a compression request that cannot fit its window. Prevents sending summarization requests that can't leave room for the output summary, with single-retry recovery on context-length rejection.

  8. #17393 — Allow description/statusMessage metadata on managed hooks. Fixes the manifest allowlist rejection in #17381.

  9. #16023 — Share resident external Workspace across sessions. Later sessions/turns reuse a Workspace-scoped binding instead of tearing it down per cycle; closing a session becomes a membership release.

  10. #17394 — Defer optional user warnings until after interactive startup. Improves perceived startup latency by showing the UI while environment checks complete, with warnings surviving redraws and /clear.

5. Hot Discussions

No Discussion data was provided in the source dataset; this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

Distilled from Issues and PRs, three dominant directions:

  1. Managed Agent / Hosted Workspace maturity — The largest cluster. Requests center on external workspace provisioning (#15512), resident workspace reuse (#16023), and channel adapters (DingTalk, #17173). Enterprises want ephemeral, session-isolated workers that behave like persistent, reusable environments.

  2. Session management & worktree parity — Codex-style worktrees are becoming a default expectation (#17228), with follow-on requests for retention/snapshots and configurable worktree roots (#17237) and sidecar-backed cold-restore indexing (#11611).

  3. Untrusted-context & injection defenses — Multiple requests converge on a systematic model of untrusted content: tracking untrusted context from shell/remote output (#17318) and sanitizing parallel-agent display surfaces (#17386).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • CI flakiness is a chronic tax. The deflake issue class (#17344, #17366, #17368, #17363, #17348, #17360, #17339) dominates recent activity, with the bot explicitly noting: if it fails again deterministically it is a real bug, not flakiness — do NOT stabilize it.

  • The Managed Agent CI gate (#14724) has been open since October with 383 comments — a long-lived, unattributed failure erodes trust in the pipeline and consumes maintainer attention.

  • Approval/render race conditions in multi-agent flows — #16425 (closed) and its sibling #17332 show recurring hangs where permission dialogs silently fail to render in batched subagent calls.

  • Security-scan backlog — #17099 tracks 29 Snyk findings across transitive npm dependencies, and #13078 shows the scheduled audit itself is unstable, leaving the project's vulnerability posture hard to assess.

  • Managed hook manifest rigidity — Closed allowlists reject standard metadata (#17381), and Claude-imported hooks retain temporary plugin paths after install (#17390) — both friction points for extension authors.

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-11-16

Issues: 499 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-11-16 00:56 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-16

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw remains in a high-velocity but stability-stressed phase. In the last 24 hours, 499 issues were updated (424 still active, 75 closed) and 500 PRs saw activity (330 open, 170 merged/closed), yet zero new releases shipped — meaning merged fixes are accumulating on main without a user-facing cut. The issue tracker is dominated by P0/P1 crash-loop, session-state, and message-loss reports, many of which are regressions from the 2026.9.x–2026.10.x line (plugin capture stalls, Windows/macOS gateway lifecycle failures, Codex/subagent completion handoff bugs). A large fraction of activity is ClawSweeper triage and roboclaw-bot/steipete maintenance PRs rather than net-new feature work, suggesting the team is in a hardening sprint. Overall activity is very high, but the ratio of unresolved P0/P1 defects to releases indicates a project under significant operational pressure.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours. No changelog, breaking-change, or migration notes to report. Notably, several fixes referenced in today's issues (e.g., the SQLite header-probe fix in 2026.11.5-beta.1) are not yet broadly reachable via openclaw update — see Issue #193962 below.

3. Project Progress

Today's merged/closed PRs (170 total) skew toward UI polish, test/CI repair, and targeted correctness fixes rather than headline features. Representative closed items:

  • #199483 (closed) — fix(ui): expired approvals claim an execution outcome — corrects misleading approval-page copy when a timeout fallback can still execute. PR #199483
  • #198813 (closed) — fix(templates): Template avatar path validates but does not resolve — fixes backslash/case-mismatched avatar paths. PR #198813
  • #198914 (closed) — fix(k8s): show deployment help without cluster access — --help no longer requires kubeconfig. PR #198914

In-flight work advancing the platform (open, ready for maintainer look):

  • #199868 fix: retain subagent results through Gateway restarts — directly targets the subagent-result-loss class dominating P1 issues. PR #199868
  • #199859 fix(knowledge): shorten write locks during large vault scans — reduces SQLite writer contention. PR #199859
  • #198070 / #198603 / #198637 — a cluster of Template "Add" UX fixes (chat opens without waiting for a plan; retryable setup; dependency-settled attach). PR #198070

Issue closures today included #193962 (P0, diamond-lobster: updater can't reach the SQLite timeout fix), #140631, #150081, #150060, #148603, #143580, #156774, #175826 — mostly stale items or ones superseded by linked PRs.

4. Community Hot Topics

Ranked by comment count:

  1. #160959 (82 comments, P0, 🦞 diamond lobster) — Gateway blocks for minutes on large external plugins (2026.9.6 regression). Issue #160959
  2. #170956 (33, P0) — Windows slow startup, unclean plugin shutdown, schtasks permission errors break restarts/updates. Issue #170956
  3. #191944 (28, P2) — macOS gateway stop fails with "Process ancestry could not be fully inspected." Issue #191944
  4. #193962 (26, P0, now closed) — Update path can't reach the SQLite header-probe fix. Issue #193962
  5. #121661 (18, P1, diamond lobster) — CLI-backed subagent announce-wake turns run tool-free; model fabricates tool calls/output. Issue #121661
  6. #143017 (17, diamond lobster) — Prompt-cache: five ways a persistent session rewrites its prefix (21.3M cache-write tokens measured). Issue #143017

Underlying needs: The top threads reveal three systemic pain clusters — (a) event-loop blocking from plugin preparation/capture (#160959, #163029, #174681, #160658 lineage), (b) platform-specific gateway lifecycle fragility on Windows/macOS (#170956, #191944, #146860, #181120), and (c) cost/context integrity (prompt-cache rewrites, usage undercounting, byte-capped transcript sliding). Users are technically sophisticated, producing wire captures and token counts, and are frustrated that multi-release regressions persist without a corrective release.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity (P0/P1 first). "Fix PR?" indicates a linked open PR exists per labels.

Severity Issue Summary Fix PR?
P0 #160959 Gateway blocks minutes capturing large external plugins (2026.9.6 regression) No new fix PR; needs maintainer review
P0 #170956 Windows slow startup, unclean shutdown, schtasks permission errors Needs info
P0 #146860 Windows managed update handoff stalls with LogonType: InteractiveToken Needs info
P0 #146791 iOS App Store build never publishes push.apns.register No — release blocker
P1 #196199 Regression since 2026.10.10: native Codex helper completions fail to resume parent (~1 in 2) Needs info
P1 #194403 Helper-completion continuations invalidate their own authority; conversations blocked No new fix PR
P1 #194451 /think and other directives mid-turn kill the turn with SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError Linked PR open
P1 #162637 Native Codex handoff fails with SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED No new fix PR
P1 #163029 2026.9.7 reloads external plugin mid-turn (40–70 s stalls) despite fix Fix-shape clear
P1 #181120 macOS Gateway hangs closing worker MessagePort (main-thread lock) No
P1 #185111 Large-session context reads scan full transcript before limits (19–25 s) Fix-shape clear
P1 #159799 Byte-capped hydration slides transcript window each turn; busts prefix caches, drops context No
P2 #191944 macOS gateway stop/--force both fail (process ancestry) Fix-shape clear
P2 #199713 Plugins → Advanced hangs mobile Chrome (renderer saturation) No
P2 #160494 Cron bound to persistent session rejected on rotation, retries re-enter rejection No

Notable regressions: #196199 and #194403 (Codex helper completion/authority) are a coherent 2026.10.10+ regression family. #163029 and #174681 are both mid-turn plugin-reload/blocking regressions despite prior fixes — suggests the fix (#172750) was reverted and the underlying design remains unresolved.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Active feature requests, with likelihood of near-term landing:

  • #197297 — Per-user secret vault (P2, needs security review) — multi-user Gateway secret isolation. Given the security-sensitive label and active PR #199863 (agent-limit enforcement), scoped host capability work is plausible soon, but the vault-as-plugin split means low near-term likelihood.
  • #166586 — Consume MCP Events and start an agent run per event (P3) — the plugin: mcp-events work (PR #199105 hardening event-date validation) signals this feature area is actively being built out.
  • #184803 — Option to disable spoken task receipt on Talk consult (P3) — small, contained; plausible in a minor release.
  • #157614 — Independent command-text limit for progress streaming (P2) — linked PR open; moderate likelihood.
  • #167341 — Operator-overridable classified failure copy (P3) — linked PR open.
  • #103067 — Centralize chat-session naming; subagent session lifetime/persistence (P2, diamond lobster) — architectural, long-running; likely roadmap-level.

Prediction: The next release will be dominated by stability restoration (plugin prep, subagent settlement, update path) rather than new features; MCP Events and Talk/streaming config are the most probable feature increments to slip in alongside.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points (dissatisfaction):

  • Update/restart reliability is the top complaint. Windows schtasks installs and macOS managed stop/update fail frequently, sometimes only succeeding "after many retries" (#170956). The update path itself cannot deliver the SQLite fix that already exists (#193962) — a compounding trust issue.
  • Performance stalls destroy usability. Minutes-long Gateway event-loop blocks from plugin preparation (#160959, #174681, #163029) and 19–25 s context reads on large sessions (#185111) make the assistant feel frozen.
  • Session/message integrity. Users report permanently blocked conversations after helper completion (#194403, #196199), silently retained zombie sessions (#160719), and transcript-window sliding that silently drops context (#159799).
  • Cost transparency. Undercounted usage for claude-cli (#148603) and unattributable child-run spend ($0.04 parent vs $14.14 child, #130257) erode operator confidence in billing.

Positive signals: Users are highly engaged and technical — many file detailed wire captures, token measurements, and exact repros. Maintainers are responsive (24h closures, linked PRs), and users credit fixes (e.g., #116461). Sentiment is best described as patient-but-strained: the community trusts the maintainers but is frustrated that long-standing regressions survive multiple releases without a correcting cut.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-unanswered or high-value items needing maintainer attention:

  • #103067 (created 2026-07-09, 10 comments, P2, diamond lobster) — Centralize session naming + subagent session lifetime/persistence. Open ~4 months; foundational for many session-state bugs. Issue #103067
  • #127195 (created 2026-08-21, 12 comments) — Sixteen call sites emit byte-identical "changed while starting work" errors with no reason code — a root-cause blocker for diagnosing the entire session-state bug family (#160494, #162637). Issue #127195
  • #121661 (created 2026-08-10, 18 comments, P1, diamond lobster) — CLI-backed subagent announce-wake turns run tool-free and fabricate output. Long-lived P1 with needs-product-decision + needs-security-review. Issue #121661
  • #118793 (created 2026-08-03, now stale) — Claude CLI session-limit errors bypass the model fallback chain. A staleness label on a failover correctness bug is a risk. Issue #118793
  • #143017 (created 2026-09-09, 17 comments, diamond lobster) — Prompt-cache prefix rewrites (21.3M cache-write tokens measured). High-cost impact, no fix PR. Issue #143017

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report: Personal AI Assistant & Agent Open-Source Ecosystem

Snapshot Date: 2026-11-16 | Projects: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw

1. Ecosystem Overview

The personal AI assistant / agent open-source landscape is bifurcated between high-velocity core platforms (OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, ZeroClaw) operating under significant operational pressure, and focused, maturing projects (IronClaw, QwenPaw) prioritizing stability over breadth. A common pattern across all five projects is a stability-stressed post-migration phase: each has recently absorbed a major architectural change (OpenClaw's 2026.9.x–10.x regressions, Hermes' unified-gateway migration #106742, QwenPaw's 2.3.0 plugin externalization, ZeroClaw's v0.9.0 line) and is now dealing with the fallout. Maintainer review bandwidth — not contributor supply — is the universal bottleneck, with open-to-merged PR ratios ranging from ~3:1 (OpenClaw) to ~24:1 (Hermes, ZeroClaw). Cost governance, credential scoping, and provider fidelity have emerged as the dominant cross-cutting concerns shaping the next release cycle.

* Health Score is a composite heuristic weighing: unresolved P0/P1 defect ratio, open-to-merged PR ratio, release cadence, and community responsiveness. It is not a measure of project quality, but of operational pressure and forward-motion clarity.

Key observations:

  • OpenClaw operates at ~10× the raw activity of any peer, but its unresolved P0/P1 backlog and zero-release window are the highest-risk signals in the dataset.
  • IronClaw is the only project with a favorable health profile — low activity but every open item has a clear next action (PR #8171 unblocks epic #2843).
  • ZeroClaw's S0 allowlist-bypass bug (#12118) with no fix PR is the single most concerning stability item across all five projects.
  • Every project has an open-to-merged PR ratio ≥ 3:1, confirming a systemic review-capacity constraint.

3. OpenClaw's Position

Advantages vs peers:

  • Ecosystem gravity: OpenClaw is the reference implementation. Peers (Hermes, ZeroClaw) are explicitly differentiated by what they do differently — OpenClaw defines the baseline for plugin APIs, gateway lifecycle, session-state, and subagent semantics.
  • Community scale: ~500 issue/PR updates/day vs Hermes' ~100 and ZeroClaw's ~77. The community produces wire captures, token measurements, and 21.3M-token prompt-cache audits (#143017) — a level of technical rigor unmatched elsewhere.
  • Plugin ecosystem maturity: ClawSweeper triage automation, roboclaw-bot maintenance PRs, and a labeled severity system (P0/P1 + 🦞 diamond lobster) indicate a scaled operations model peers lack.
  • Feature surface: Subagent settlement, prompt caching, MCP events, Talk consult, and cron/session integration are all in active development — broader than IronClaw's cost-focused scope or QwenPaw's channel-centric focus.

Technical approach differences:

  • OpenClaw leans on a plugin-first, event-loop-centric architecture, which is simultaneously its greatest strength (extensibility) and its greatest liability (event-loop blocking from plugin prep, #160959, #174681).
  • Peers diverge: Hermes is migrating toward a unified gateway with multiplexed profiles; ZeroClaw is investing heavily in scoped credential primitives (Rust-native SSH broker, write-only TLS creds); QwenPaw uses a plugin externalization model that proved regression-prone in 2.3.0.
  • OpenClaw is platform-broad (Windows/macOS/iOS/K8s), whereas peers are narrower (Hermes Desktop-centric, IronClaw server-oriented, QwenPaw channel-centric with Feishu/WeChat).

Community size comparison:

  • OpenClaw ≫ ZeroClaw > Hermes > QwenPaw > IronClaw in raw engagement.
  • However, OpenClaw's ratio of P0/P1 to releases is the worst in the cohort — scale is not translating to user-perceived stability.

Strategic implication: OpenClaw's moat is ecosystem position and community scale; its vulnerability is trust erosion from long-surviving regressions without corrective releases (#193962 update-path failure is the canonical example).

4. Shared Technical Focus Areas

Four requirements emerge across three or more projects, signaling ecosystem-wide gaps:

Theme Projects Specific Needs
Cost governance & USD budgeting OpenClaw (#130257, #148603), IronClaw (#2843, #8171), ZeroClaw (#9816, #12477, #12353), Hermes (#122094) USD-denominated budgets cascading user→project→mission→thread; accurate pricing tables; prompt-cache keep-alive; cost visibility per conversation. The single strongest cross-project signal.
Credential / secret scoping ZeroClaw (#12402, #12408, #12418, #12422), Hermes (#92424, #146318, #147720), OpenClaw (#197297 per-user secret vault), IronClaw (#8173) Write-only credentials, per-profile/per-agent secret isolation, scoped HTTP/SSH transports, provider-agnostic failover.
Session / profile state integrity OpenClaw (#103067, #194403, #196199), Hermes (#143150, #155955, #156258), QwenPaw (#8746, #8757), ZeroClaw (#12289) Session ownership reconciliation, silent-fork prevention, resumable sessions post-migration, disabled-agent enforcement.
Provider fidelity (timeouts, context, signatures) ZeroClaw (#12014, #12401, #10884, #7899), IronClaw (#8172), Hermes (#143065, #68263), OpenClaw (#118793) Configurable idle timeouts for local LLMs, accurate context-window discovery, thinking-signature preservation, honoring max_tokens/budget_tokens on compatible endpoints.
Delegation security / least-privilege ZeroClaw (#11138), Hermes (#91505, #92424), OpenClaw (#121661), QwenPaw (#8755) Caller tool-level approval inheritance, scoped approval tokens, per-agent credential scoping, path-scoped file access.

Interpretation: These five themes are not independent — they form a "trust layer" stack: users cannot deploy agents in shared/multi-tenant environments without cost control + credential isolation + state integrity + provider fidelity + delegation policy. No single project has solved all five; each leads in one.

Notable divergence: ZeroClaw is the only project where security primitives are the primary feature axis (not an add-on). Hermes is the only project with a coherent protocol-compatibility strategy (ACP 1.0, MCP, A2A). IronClaw is the only project where a single epic (#2843) defines the roadmap. QwenPaw is the only project explicitly declining multi-user support (#8751) despite structural demand — a positioning bet.

6. Community Momentum & Maturity

Activity tiers:

  • Tier 1 — High-velocity, hardening (OpenClaw): ~500 daily updates; mature tooling (ClawSweeper, roboclaw-bot); massive contributor base. Momentum: high; Maturity: high; Risk: operational.
  • Tier 2 — Mid-velocity, migration-recovering (Hermes, ZeroClaw): ~50 daily updates each; strong contributor interest but review-constrained. Hermes is post-migration; ZeroClaw is mid-security-roadmap. Momentum: medium-high; Maturity: medium; Risk: review backlog.
  • Tier 3 — Low-velocity, focused (IronClaw, QwenPaw): ~3–12 daily updates; clear scoped priorities; small maintainer teams. Momentum: low-medium; Maturity: medium; Risk: aging backlog.

Rapidly iterating: OpenClaw (feature + fix churn), ZeroClaw (credential PR cluster advancing). Stabilizing: Hermes (post-#106742 cleanup), QwenPaw (post-2.3.0 same-day fix PRs). Quietly maturing: IronClaw (deliberate, dependency-gated roadmap).

Maturity signals by project:

  • OpenClaw: Highest process maturity (severity labels, automated triage, linked-PR discipline) but release-discipline gap — merged fixes accumulate on main unreachable via openclaw update.
  • Hermes: Strong protocol-layer maturity (ACP/MCP/A2A PRs) but desktop-state maturity gap (silent chat forks, frozen windows).
  • IronClaw: Highest operational maturity — every open item has a clear unblock path.
  • QwenPaw: Strong contributor responsiveness (same-day fix PRs) but review/merge bottleneck (12 open PRs, 0 merges).
  • ZeroClaw: Strong architectural ambition (Rust-native SSH, scoped creds) but security-invariant enforcement gap (#12118 allowlist bypass, #12289 disabled-agent execution).

7. Trend Signals

Seven industry trends extracted from cross-project community feedback, ranked by signal strength:

1. Cost governance is the #1 unmet need. Four of five projects have active cost-related threads. Users are moving past "token counting" toward USD-denominated, hierarchically-cascading budgets (IronClaw #2843) with accurate pricing (IronClaw #8171, up to 8× off) and prompt-cache economics (OpenClaw #143017: 21.3M cache-write tokens measured; Hermes #122094 keep-alive). Value for developers: ship a pricing table + budget cascade early; stale pricing destroys trust in every cost feature downstream.

2. Credential scoping is becoming table-stakes for multi-tenant agents. ZeroClaw's scoped-credential RFC (#12422) and PR cluster, Hermes' path-scoped profile access (#92424), and OpenClaw's per-user secret vault (#197297) all point the same direction: agents must operate under least-privilege, per-scope credentials — not shared process-wide secrets. Value: design credential primitives before multi-user features; retrofitting is expensive.

3. Provider fidelity is a silent trust-killer. Users repeatedly report configuration not honored — silent 32k context fallbacks (ZeroClaw #12014), ignored max_tokens (Hermes #68263), no-op /reasoning on compatible endpoints (#143065), and hardcoded watchdogs killing slow local LLMs (IronClaw #8172). Value: loud, explicit errors on unsupported configuration beat silent defaults; document provider-capability matrices.

4. Silent failures are the most damaging failure class. Across projects, the highest-severity user complaints are invisible — WeChat polling dying with "healthy" status (QwenPaw #8757), tasks swallowed during startup (#8746), Anthropic cost silently $0.00 (ZeroClaw #9816), false-success GPU jobs billing indefinitely (Hermes #156278). Value: invest in liveness assertions and "did the agent actually do anything?" telemetry.

5. Session/profile state is the new frontier of complexity. Post-migration state bugs dominate Hermes (#143150, #155955, #156258), OpenClaw (#103067, #194403, #196199), and QwenPaw (#8755). Users expect resumable, non-forking, profile-scoped sessions as a baseline. Value: treat session ownership as a first-class, centralized concern (cf. OpenClaw #103067 backlog item) rather than per-feature state.

6. Local/self-hosted LLM support is a distinct user segment with distinct needs. Ollama (IronClaw #8172, #8173), MiniMax/Anthropic-compatible endpoints (Hermes #143065), and custom OpenAI-compatible providers (ZeroClaw #12014) all surface timeout, context-discovery, and fallback requirements that cloud-first designs miss. Value: make idle timeouts, context windows, and failover provider-agnostic from day one.

7. Review bandwidth — not contributor supply — is the ecosystem-wide constraint. Open-to-merged PR ratios: OpenClaw ~2:1 (best), Hermes ~16:1, ZeroClaw ~24:1, QwenPaw ~12:1, IronClaw ~1:0 (n=1). Several XL PRs (#129388 OpenClaw, #11847/#11869 ZeroClaw, #6325 QwenPaw) have sat for weeks-to-months. Value: projects that solve review throughput (automated proof checks, scoped reviewers, smaller PR norms) will outpace peers regardless of feature ambition.

Bottom line for technical decision-makers: The ecosystem has converged on a shared "trust layer" requirement stack (cost, credentials, state, provider fidelity, delegation), but no single project has solved it. OpenClaw offers the broadest ecosystem and community; IronClaw the cleanest roadmap discipline; ZeroClaw the most ambitious security architecture; Hermes the strongest protocol coverage; QwenPaw the deepest channel integration. Choose based on which trust-layer dimension is your hard requirement — and expect every project to spend the next release cycle on stability restoration rather than net-new features.

  1. High — #8172 [qa-bug]: PRIMARY_MODEL_CALL_IDLE_TIMEOUT is not configurable, causing slow local LLM (Ollama) calls to be killed by the agent-loop idle watchdog. Reproducible on hosted-staging v1.4.1. No fix PR yet.
  2. Medium — #8173: Failover is effectively broken for registry providers — the fallback provider is always constructed as a NEAR AI provider regardless of configuration. No fix PR yet.
  3. Low — #8171: Not a runtime bug, but stale pricing data in model_cost() constitutes a correctness/data-accuracy issue with downstream impact on budget enforcement. Fix PR is open.

No crashes or regressions were reported today.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • Cost-based USD budgeting (#2843) is the strongest roadmap signal — it's an enhancement scoped across agent, DB, and config, and today's pricing PR (#8171) was explicitly framed as a prerequisite. Expect this to land in an upcoming minor release.
  • Provider-agnostic failover (#8173) and configurable idle timeouts (#8172) are likely near-term candidates for a 1.4.x patch or 1.5 release, given they are small, targeted, and QA-flagged.
  • The cascade model in #2843 (user → project → mission → thread → sub-thread) suggests future work on hierarchical budget enforcement and reporting.

7. User Feedback Summary

  • Pain point — cost opacity: Users are hitting iteration/time caps that don't reflect real spend; demand for USD-denominated budgets is clear and organizational (multi-tenant, multi-project).
  • Pain point — local LLM support: Ollama users face two distinct failures: hardcoded timeouts and broken fallback construction. This is a recurring theme for self-hosted deployments.
  • Pain point — stale pricing: Reported prices diverging from provider reality (up to ~8× off for some models) undermines trust in any cost-tracking feature.
  • Satisfaction signals: No negative sentiment on core functionality; feedback is constructive and feature-oriented, indicating an engaged and technically sophisticated user base.

8. Backlog Watch

  • #2843 — Open since 2026-04-22, only 1 comment despite being a high-risk, multi-scope enhancement. With a dependency PR now open (#8171), maintainers should prioritize review and add design feedback to keep the epic moving.
  • #8171 — Small but blocking; needs maintainer review/merge to unblock #2843.
  • #8172 and #8173 — Fresh QA issues with no assignee or linked PR; both are low-effort fixes that should be triaged promptly to avoid aging into the backlog.

Data source: github.com/nearai/ironclaw — snapshot for 2026-11-16. Activity level: low; attention recommended on pending PR #8171 and triage of #8172/#8173.

QwenPaw — agentscope-ai/QwenPaw

QwenPaw Project Digest — 2026-11-16

1. Today's Overview

QwenPaw is in an intense post-2.3.0 stabilization phase: 12 issues and 12 PRs were updated in the last 24h, but zero PRs were merged or closed, leaving all 12 open PRs in review limbo. The activity is heavily bug-driven — many reports are regressions introduced by the 2.3.0 release (Feishu channel, Console notifications, channel credential scoping), suggesting quality debt accumulated during the plugin externalization refactor (#8187). Encouragingly, community contributors have already submitted fix PRs for most of the newly reported bugs the same day they were filed, indicating a responsive contributor base. However, the absence of merges and releases today, combined with a growing open-PR backlog (~12), flags a review/merge bottleneck as the primary project-health risk.

2. Releases

None. No new releases in the last 24h (current stable: v2.3.0; main carries version 2.3.1b1).

No PRs were merged or closed today. However, two issues were closed:

  • [CLOSED] #8751 — Multi-user support request; closed with confirmation that QwenPaw remains single-user by design (auth router enforces one account). Link

4. Community Hot Topics

Item Comments Signal
#8361 — memory_search loop blocked replies (CLOSED) 4 Highest-engagement issue; core agent-loop reliability matters most to users
#8747 — Checkpoints nav entry missing in v2.3.0 console 2 UI regression tied to removed core.agent-group parentId; feature works but is undiscoverable

#8751 — Multi-user support (CLOSED) 2 Strong latent demand; declined by design

Underlying needs: Users are pushing QwenPaw toward multi-agent, multi-channel, shared-installation deployments (two WeChat bots, subagents, checkpoints). The 2.3.0 design (single-user auth, per-process credential scoping) is colliding with these expectations — a sign the product is outgrowing its single-user origin.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity:

  1. Message-dropping / silent failure (critical)

    • #8746 — Tasks submitted during background startup are silently swallowed: agent builds but never calls the LLM, no error logged. Model-agnostic (Console + Feishu, Windows 11). No fix PR yet.

  2. Channel/credential correctness (high)

    • #8748 — Feishu reconnect supervisor exits permanently when disconnect cleanup raises; connection never recovers. Fix PR: #8749.

    • #8747 — Checkpoints nav entry missing (parentId points to removed core.agent-group). Backend/route fine; pure navigation regression. No fix PR yet.

    • #8630 — Partial channel updates silently reset omitted fields (e.g., enabled turned off with no warning) — a stability-adjacent data-loss bug with a pending fix.

Assessment: The 2.3.0 Feishu/WeChat plugin externalization (#8187) introduced a cluster of channel-lifecycle regressions. Positively, ~4 of 6 channel bugs have same-day community fix PRs. The two silent-failure bugs (#8746, #8757) remain unfixed and deserve maintainer priority.

    • Multi-agent/credential sharing friction (#8755) — a shared desktop frontend with two WeChat bots is a genuine household/SMB pattern; upgrades broke it.
    • Notification noise from subagents (#8736) and undiscoverable features (#8747).
    • Regression fatigue: #8752 is a repeat of a previously fixed bug (#4600), which users explicitly called out.
  • Use cases observed: family-shared installations with per-person agents and WeChat bots; enterprise PoCs (Italian aerospace, corporate deployment); Feishu/WeChat as primary channels; long-running background startup workflows.

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-16

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw shows high issue and PR churn with very low closure throughput on 2026-11-16: 27 issues were updated (all still open, zero closed) and 50 PRs were touched (48 open, only 2 merged/closed), with no new releases. The issue tracker is dominated by S1/S2 provider and runtime regressions — notably cost accounting failures (#9816), context-window fallback logic (#12014), and Anthropic thinking-signature breakage (#12401) — suggesting the recent v0.9.0 line introduced meaningful instability. Activity is heavily concentrated around a single prolific contributor (CastelloBrancoTecnologia) driving large XL security/credential PRs, while several high-severity bugs sit with fix PRs unmerged. Overall health assessment: active but congested — strong community engagement and a clear security roadmap, but maintainer review bandwidth appears to be the bottleneck.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours. No migration notes or breaking-change advisories to report.

3. Project Progress

Only 2 PRs were merged/closed in the last 24h (identities not exposed in the dataset), so no headline features landed today. However, the pipeline shows substantial work in flight:

  • Scoped credential & secret management — a coherent multi-PR effort is advancing: write-only plugin TLS credentials (#12402), scoped HTTP credentials (#12408), and task-owned SSH transports using scoped credentials (#12418), all building on the RFC in #12422.
  • Native Rust SSH task broker (#12438) — replaces Python/tomli/cryptography dependencies while keeping OpenSSH as transport owner.
  • Browser voice for OIDC sessions (#12459) extending paired-device voice settings (#12269).
  • Channel reliability fixes — preserving completed tool results (#11911), progress reporting during long turns (#11874), and requiring message content for background send_via (#11859).
  • Runtime hygiene — binding cached HTTP clients to their Tokio runtime (#12323), addressing #12236.

Net: features are advancing but not landing; the merge queue is stalled relative to creation rate.

4. Community Hot Topics

Ranked by comment count among recently updated items:

Item Comments Link Underlying Need
#12014 — Custom OpenAI-compatible provider assumes 32,000 context window 6 Issue #12014 Users need accurate model-capacity discovery; silent fallbacks that reject valid turns erode trust in custom providers.
#9816 — Anthropic provider reports $0.00 spend, budget caps never fire 6 Issue #9816 Cost governance is broken — operators cannot enforce spend limits, a compliance/security concern.
#12401 — keep_tool_context_turns breaks Claude Opus 5.5 with thinking-signature 400 5 Issue #12401 Multi-turn tool use with reasoning models is core workflow; context-collapse logic conflicts with Anthropic's signature requirements.
#8541 — Matrix thread/conversation-scoped history 4 Issue #8541 Channel users want conversation boundaries matching native chat semantics.
#11138 — Caller tool-level approval in bounded delegation 4 Issue #11138 Security policy inheritance across delegated agents — a governance gap.

Analysis: The hot list reveals two dominant community concerns: (a) provider fidelity — context windows, cost, and reasoning-signature handling must match upstream semantics exactly; and (b) security policy composition — approvals, credentials, and delegation boundaries need a coherent model rather than per-feature patches.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity (S0 highest):

S0 — Security / Allowlist Bypass

  • #12118 — cmd.exe dialect resolves bare commands from workspace first, so a workspace-written git.bat runs as allowlisted git. Link — No fix PR identified; critical sandbox escape vector.

S1 — Workflow Blocked

  • #12014 — Context-window fallback to 32,000 rejects valid turns. Link
  • #9816 — Anthropic cost always $0.00; budget caps inert. Link (status:in-progress)
  • #12401 — Thinking-signature 400 after tool-context collapse. Link
  • #10901 — Mattermost drops first DM message. Link
  • #12477 — cost.enforcement.mode ignored; budget always stops turn even in "warn". Link — New today.

S2 — Degraded Behavior

  • #10884 — Streaming 300s idle timeout not configurable. Link (in-progress)
  • #7899 — OpenAI STT ignores env credentials. Link
  • #12390 — Shell tool swallows stderr on non-zero exit. Link
  • #12288 — "Discard all" retains drafts a later save persists. Link
  • #12330 — zerocode silently falls back to local daemon on config parse error. Link
  • #12289 — Disabled agents still run turns via operator chat/RPC. Link
  • #12413 / #12412 — OpenCode Go context discovery fails; wrong model catalogue used. Links
  • #12476 — Gateway logs every connection at INFO via spawn!, flooding traces. Link — New today.

S3 — Minor

  • #12236 — Cached HTTP clients shared across test runtimes. Link — Fix PR #12323 open.

Notable: No confirmed fix PRs are linked to the S0/S1 bugs, aside from #12236→#12323. This is a stability red flag.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Active feature requests, clustered by theme:

  • Credential & secret scoping: #12373 (write-only WebUI credential management), #12422 (RFC: scoped operator-managed service credentials), #12447 (Wazuh tool with scoped credentials). Strongly aligned with the credential PR cluster (#12402, #12408, #12418).
  • Cost visibility: #12353 (running estimated cost per conversation) — pairs with the broken cost ledger (#9816) and enforcement bug (#12477).
  • Identity propagation: #12441 (deliver requesting user's identity to tool execution) — enables multi-user assistant deployments.
  • Web search defaults: #12480 (decide default search provider and disclosure) — privacy/UX concern.
  • Channel semantics: #8541 (Matrix thread-scoped history).
  • Delegation security: #11138 (caller tool-level approval inheritance).

Prediction for next version: The credential/secret scoping stack is the most mature and cohesive; expect write-only credential management and scoped SSH/HTTP credentials to be the headline feature. The cost ledger is likely a must-fix given #9816 and #12477 both concern the same subsystem. Identity propagation (#12441) is foundational and may land early if adopted.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points (dissatisfaction drivers):

  • Trust in provider behavior: Multiple users report silent fallbacks (32k context), silent zero-costs, and hard failures (thinking-signature 400). The common thread is configuration not being honored — the system substitutes defaults without loud warnings.
  • Cost governance gap: Users explicitly cannot enforce budgets (#9816, #12477), undermining the "spending allowance" use case they are designing around.
  • Security posture: The git.bat allowlist bypass (#12118) and disabled-agent execution (#12289) indicate that security invariants aren't enforced uniformly across entry points.
  • Diagnostics quality: Shell tool swallowing stderr (#12390) and gateway INFO-log flooding (#12476) frustrate debugging.

Satisfaction signals: Contributors are actively proposing and building sophisticated security features (scoped credentials, task-owned SSH brokers), suggesting the project's architecture is extensible and the community trusts its direction — even as they hit stability walls.

Long-unanswered or slow-moving items warranting maintainer attention:

  • #11869 / #11868 (PRs, created 2026-10-19) — Task-owned SSH transport and repeated-call closeout; both size:XL awaiting review. Links

Maintainer bottleneck: The XL PRs from CastelloBrancoTecnologia (SSH, XMPP, credentials) are consistently flagged needs-maintainer-review or needs-author-action and have been open for weeks. Combined with the ~48:2 open-to-merged ratio today, review capacity — not contribution volume — is the limiting factor on ZeroClaw's velocity.

item.content:encoded:
AI Infrastructure Digest 2026-11-16

Generated: 2026-11-16 00:56 UTC | Projects covered: 6

  • vLLM
  • SGLang
  • llama.cpp
  • Ollama
  • LiteLLM
  • Unsloth

Cross-Project Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — AI Infrastructure Ecosystem

Snapshot date: 2026-11-16

1. Ecosystem Overview

The stack is splitting cleanly along maturity lines: serving engines (vLLM, SGLang) are consolidating around a stability narrative — vLLM's Rust frontend roadmap and SGLang's explicit "1.0 = no silent config changes" tracker both signal that feature velocity is giving way to compatibility guarantees. Meanwhile, the local-runtime layer (llama.cpp, Ollama) is racing on multimodal breadth — TTS, STT, and vision landed in a single day at llama.cpp — while remaining exposed to per-hardware regressions (V100, HIP, Vulkan, SYCL). The gateway layer (LiteLLM) is quietly rewriting its critical path in Rust (budgets, Bedrock invoke) even as streaming-correctness bugs persist across Anthropic/Responses/Bedrock translation surfaces. Training (Unsloth) had the most consequential correctness day: a silent MoE router aux-loss gradient drop under gradient checkpointing, plus FSDP2/DDP hardening — the kind of bug that produces plausible-looking loss curves and undertrained models. Across all six projects, the dominant risk theme is silent failure: wrong activations, dropped gradients, collapsed cache hits, and accepted-but-corrupted tool calls, rather than crashes.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Layer Issues (active/tracked) PRs (active) Releases (24h) Notable status
vLLM Serving engine High (many long-context + correctness) Very high (spec-dec, NVFP4, KV offload) None Rust frontend experimental; llguidance now mandatory (#66345)
SGLang Serving engine 43 418 None 1.0 tracker (#50045); Unified Memory roadmap (#49944)
llama.cpp Local runtime High (HW-specific regressions) High 7 builds (b12419–b12428) Jinja revert/reland; multimodal surge
Ollama Local runtime Moderate (some high-severity open) Moderate None VRAM accounting fix in flight (#19632)
LiteLLM Gateway High (streaming correctness) Moderate–high v1.111.0-dev.4 Keyless Sigstore signing (breaking for CI)
Unsloth Fine-tuning Moderate Very high (maintainer PR wave) None Silent MoE grad bug fixed (#17873)

Read: SGLang shows the highest raw PR volume (418); llama.cpp is the only project shipping releases today; Unsloth's PR density reflects a concentrated correctness push rather than feature expansion.

3. Model Support Race

Model / Arch vLLM SGLang llama.cpp Ollama LiteLLM Unsloth
GLM-5.3 / Flash ✅ KDA via FlashInfer (#63544), Hopper decode (#67536) ⚠️ Chat template fix requested (#50408) — — — —
Kimi-K3.1-Pro ✅ MI355X recipe (#67817) ⚠️ mxfp4 activation bug (#45755, closed) — — — —
MiniMax-M3.1 ✅ B200/B300 decode (#65483) — ✅ mainline (#32301) — — —
DeepSeek-V4.1 ✅ ROCm MegaMoE (#67584) ✅ Ascend NPU cookbook ⚠️ Vulkan -fa 1 bug — — ✅ training fixes (#17881)
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next ✅ (TP parity) — — — — ✅ SFT packing (#17827)
Zonos3-mini TTS — — ✅ (#32020) — — —
Higgs v3 / VibeVoice-ASR — — ✅ (#32329) — — —
Gemma 4 vision — — — ⚠️ Windows broken (#16532) — ✅ decode graphs (#17871)
Vertex Meta Muse — — — — ✅ (#50768) —
AxForge — — — — ✅ (#51865) —

Who's ahead:

  • Serving engines: vLLM leads decisively on frontier-LLM performance support (GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3.1, MiniMax-M3.1 specialized decode paths). SGLang lags on model-specific kernels but is ahead on hardware diversity (Ascend NPU, gfx1250, gfx942 EAGLE).
  • Local runtime: llama.cpp is the clear winner on multimodal breadth — it shipped TTS + STT + ASR + vision in 24h, and is the only project adding new modality classes.
  • Gateway: LiteLLM is expanding the provider matrix (Vertex Muse, AxForge) rather than model architectures.
  • Training: Unsloth leads on DeepSeek-V4.1 and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next trainability, but its inference-side regression (UD 3.1 GGUFs + mismatched MTP heads, acceptance 74%→56–66%, #17402) is the standout open item.

4. Performance Frontier

Optimization axis Where the effort is concentrated
KV cache & memory tiering vLLM: KV-offload DMA thresholds (#57555), encoder-cache events (#67030). SGLang: Unified Memory roadmap collapsing full-attn KV + SWA + recurrent state into one arena (#49944); HiCache/Mamba host pooling (#45400, #47867). Ollama: context-shift RoPE drift (#19680).
Speculative decoding vLLM: top-k/top-p cutoffs at logits load (#66534), K0 spec-window release (#66169). SGLang: EAGLE on gfx942 (#49883). llama.cpp: HIP draft-MTP prefill collapse (~80%, #31495). Unsloth: MTP head mismatch regression (#17402).
Quantization vLLM: NVFP4 validation, ModelOpt 52 GiB RAM bug (#46268), GLM-5.3 online quant (#64373), MXFP4 CPU fallback (#61346).
Kernels llama.cpp: SYCL fast-division (#32213), Grouped XMX GEMM (#31428), HIP stream_k (#30022), OpenCL FA kernel (#32302). vLLM: FlashInfer MoE workspace reuse (#62948). SGLang: fast_topk overflow fix (#38144).
Distributed / disaggregated serving SGLang: PD-disaggregation correctness (#39846, #39764, #50547), gfx1250 custom all-reduce (#50660). vLLM: ROCm DP-group routing (#67584).
Tokenizer / TTFT floor SGLang: toktier chunk-parallel backend (#44374) — the clearest TTFT signal today (100K-token Qwen3-8B turn still pays single-core CPU cost).
Gateway hot path LiteLLM: Rust budget engine (#51535), priority queueing on 429/529 (#51892), cache-key double-stringify regression (#51935).
Training step time Unsloth: block-compile recompile storm (#17864), vision mask-divergence stalls (#17880), GKD teacher placement (#17876).

Takeaway: Serving engines are optimizing down the memory hierarchy (KV offload → host tier → unified arena), while local runtimes are still fighting kernel-level and hardware-specific wins. The gateway's frontier is admission control, not inference.

5. Layer Positioning

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  GATEWAY / CONTROL PLANE      LiteLLM                            │
│  routing, budgets, provider normalization, spend, auth           │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  SERVING ENGINES              vLLM        SGLang                 │
│  high-throughput GPU serving, PD-disagg, KV/prefix cache,        │
│  spec decode, multi-tenant production                            │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  LOCAL RUNTIME                llama.cpp   Ollama                 │
│  single-node / edge, GGUF, multimodal, hardware breadth,         │
│  developer ergonomics                                            │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  TRAINING / FINE-TUNING       Unsloth                            │
│  LoRA/QLoRA, GRPO, FSDP2/DDP, quantization-aware training        │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  • vLLM vs SGLang — Direct competitors, diverging on strategy: vLLM pursues frontier-model kernels + a Rust frontend; SGLang pursues a stability contract (1.0) and unified memory. Both are targeting the same production deployment.
  • llama.cpp vs Ollama — llama.cpp is the engine (breadth, kernels, multimodal); Ollama is the productized runtime (model management, OpenAI-compatible API, VRAM heuristics). Ollama's issues (reranking #3368, tool-call parser #19705) are product-layer; llama.cpp's are engine-layer.
  • LiteLLM — Sits above all of them; its correctness bugs (streaming usage undercount, reasoning-model mis-encoding) propagate to every downstream app regardless of which engine serves the request.
  • Unsloth — Orthogonal: it produces the artifacts (GGUFs, adapters) that the runtime and serving layers consume. The MTP head mismatch (#17402) is a cross-layer bug — a training-side artifact regression that surfaces as an inference-side throughput loss.

6. Trend Signals

Signal 1 — "Silent failure" is the dominant risk class

  • Unsloth: MoE router aux-loss gradient dropped with no error (#17873) — loss curve looked normal.
  • SGLang: Kimi-K3 mxfp4 silently computed GPT-OSS SwiGLU instead of SiTU (#45755).
  • vLLM: glm47 tool parser silently drops calls with unknown function names (#67684).
  • llama.cpp: Vulkan all-NaN logits (#31509), control vectors diverging via KV (#32341).
  • Ollama: Qwen tool-call argument corruption depending on stream chunking (#19705).

Implication: Validation must be output-aware, not status-code-aware. Teams should build client-side semantic checks (tool-call shape, logit sanity, cache-hit assertions) rather than trusting 200 responses.

Signal 2 — Rust is entering the critical path of the control plane

  • vLLM: Rust frontend (VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1, experimental, #44280).
  • SGLang: Rust server + sgl-router (#48170, #50151).
  • LiteLLM: callbacks-budgets crate, Rust-only Bedrock invoke (#51330, #51535).

Implication: Expect a bifurcation where the data plane stays Python (for kernel ecosystem) and the control plane migrates to Rust for latency and safety. Budget/auth/signing logic will be the first to move.

Signal 3 — Long-context + MoE + hybrid state is a fragile combination

  • vLLM: Kimi-K3 NaN-logit poisoning after ~240K prefill persists across requests (#51039).
  • SGLang: HiCache host hits collapse to zero on hybrid GDN after ~3 long prefixes (#45400).
  • vLLM: Long-prefill decode starvation on GB10 (#62574); --prefix-match-unit costs ~30ms TTFT (#67674).

Implication: Isolate long-context traffic to dedicated replicas; do not co-locate with latency-sensitive short-context traffic. Measure host-tier cache hit rates under multi-prefix load, not single-prefix tests.

Signal 4 — Multimodal local serving is becoming real

llama.cpp shipped TTS (Zonos3-mini), STT (Higgs v3, VibeVoice-ASR), and ASR in one day; Fish S2 and Inkling 1 are in review. A full audio loop (STT → LLM → TTS) is now plausible in a single llama-server process.

Implication: Voice-agent developers can prototype entirely local. But watch Ollama's Windows Gemma 4 vision bug (#16532) and Unsloth's diffusion-tool-call immaturity (#17815) — vision/tool integration is not production-ready on all runtimes.

Signal 5 — Signing and supply-chain policy is a migration event

LiteLLM moved to keyless Sigstore signing (#v1.111.0-dev.3+), breaking cosign verify --key. Ollama decoupled MLX-C/XGrammar for packagers (#19688). SGLang bumped pulldown-cmark for a RUSTSEC advisory.

Implication: CI/CD verification pipelines are a breaking-change surface as much as APIs. Treat signing policy changes as upgrade blockers and audit before adopting new minor versions.

Signal 6 — Budget/admission control is not yet a hard guarantee

LiteLLM: max_budget_per_session can be exceeded under concurrency (#34732); spend-log batches drop (#33873); streaming usage undercounted (#36114).

Implication: If you have financial or quota guarantees, enforce them at your gateway layer, not LiteLLM's. The Rust budget engine (#51535) is intended to close this gap — track it, but don't assume it's shipped.

  • Tool-calling is not yet safe to trust blindly. Two open bugs (#67684, #64326) cause silently dropped or spuriously injected tool calls for GLM-5.3 Flash deployments. 6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Two structural changes are coming, both aimed at you. SGLang 1.0 (#50045) will start erroring on configs it currently accepts silently. Audit your launch flags and config files against the eventual upgrade notes before you're forced to. Unified Memory (#49944) promises to end fixed KV/state partitioning — good for mixed workloads, but it changes memory-capacity planning and OOM behavior.
  • Tokenizer is your hidden TTFT tax on multi-turn agents. The 100K-token Qwen3-8B data point in #44373 is the clearest number today: radix caching helps the model, not the tokenizer. If you re-send full history every turn, benchmark toktier in staging and consider prompt-structure changes (fewer, larger messages) as a stopgap.
  • Long-context + hybrid Mamba/GDN + HiCache is a fragile combination right now. #45400 shows host-tier hits silently collapsing after a few long prefixes due to Mamba pool exhaustion. If you run long-context serving on Qwen3.5/GDN-class models with --hicache-*, measure host hit rates under realistic multi-prefix load, not single-prefix tests. The proposed --hicache-mamba-size-gb flag (#47867, open) is the intended remedy — track it.
  • Audit your Responses API path if you serve coding agents. #42110 causes replayed Codex turns to split into multiple assistant blocks, teaching the model to terminate before tool calls. This is the kind of bug that looks like a model-quality problem but is a serving bug. Verify against your own tool-call traces.
  • Verify closures, don't trust them. A large fraction of today's issues are [CLOSED] [inactive], which here functions as a housekeeping label, not a "fixed" label — several (the bootstrap auth issue #39400, the silent mxfp4 activation bug #45755) describe real defects whose fixes are unclear. Treat "inactive" as "unresolved but deprioritized" in your risk register.
  • AMD/ROCm users get real TPOT traction. #50665 removes a known host-sync regression on MI355, and #49883 defaults EAGLE verify to unified_attention on gfx942. Both are open; test them before adopting.
